title: Unfocused
body:
For an app that is supposed to make chaotic people more focused and productive this things is surprisingly avoid of structure.

The onboarding is terrible with selecting a few tasks and it then dropping you into the app with ZERO GUIDANCE of what to do. After playing around with it it’s basically a todo list with some cute animations and an AI that is dumber than a rock. It could not even remove a morning routine that was useless after telling it I don’t need it cause it’s 5 PM.

I then went ahead and tried the morning routine for fun at 5 PM and after I completed all the tasks the button sends you back to the timer screen where you can start a new senseless timer instead of putting you back to the app.

All features like the todo list and the AI are accessible even without premium or any free trial making it impossible to even know what premium even does let alone the buy screen is spending more time listing pointless awards instead of showing you the features.

App of the year 2025? Absolute joke and this award can no longer be taken seriously!

title: Great idea, buggy realisation
body:
I love the app - in theory.

As an autistic person, I really appreciate Tiimo for creating this visual scheduling app with beautiful interface (esp. compared to similar apps on the market).
It would be an irreplaceable asset in my life IF it weren't for the bugs!
The phone widget does not sync reliably if the app is not opened regularly. 
The watch app is even worse and does not work reliably -period.

For people who have enough executive functioning ability to open up their scheduling app regularly anyways this shouldn't be too much of a problem.
For me and other people who have exactly the problem that they struggle with planning and starting, an app that relies on the prime initiative of their users does not do a lot.

I originally got the app to get reminders on my watch e.g. when I am in focus mode and not checking my phone for hours. 
Since the idea is still great and good things need support, I will keep paying for the app for a bit and see how it will develop over the next months.
But right now it is not the aid it should be.

(Tiimos customer support is great, but naturally they can't fix those major technical issues)

title: This actually works
body:
I have tried lots of planners, but they always seem usable for a day or two, and then - the next thing you know - you realise that you haven’t used it for a week…

I had the version with the AI integration, and I think this is what makes it work so well. By asking it to create a task, you need to give it some details about the task itself… then you can ask it to create subtasks. <— this is where the magic happens. By breaking it down into potential tasks that are close enough to make you think about what they actually need to be, you end up properly planning the detailed steps and checking them off one by one. 

This has been massive for me. I’ve been using it for a month - for work tasks and basic everyday tasks and it’s a game changer. 

It’s especially great if your someone who humps from one task to another like I do. ADHDers, this one’s a dream!

author: ripple effect reducing

title: Slick, well-priced, but not really helpful.
body:
This review is based on a short, few-days free trial. 

First I have to say that I love the notes widget. I almost paid for the app just for that. If it didn’t ‘vanish’ the objectives achieved one checked off, I probably would have. 

For the rest…. The UI is slick. Everything works smoothly and well. Unfortunately, it’s not really helpful. Here are the main reasons why: 

1: It doesn’t make noise at you to do the thing you’d planned to do. (My phone does spend most time on DND  to help prevent distractions - but all push notifications for this app were enabled. It made no difference. Also even when I saw a notification, it just assumes you’re doing it so it doesn’t bother you once it starts the timer.).

2: If you missed the thing you’d planned to do (aka not ticked it off at the end of the scheduled time) it doesn’t agitate at you to do it later that day in a free space. 

3: While it does offer ‘pause’ or ‘reschedule’, it doesn’t offer any kind of ‘not today’ or ‘chose not to do’ option. It might sound silly, but when I don’t go to scheduled work because of a public holiday or illness, I want the app to track it differently to something I just failed to motivate myself to do.

4: Want to create something similar but different? (For eg birthdays or second or third job schedules.) There’s no ‘duplicate’ option. Every single one must be created manually, even if you want the same reminders and checklists, just on different dates. 

5: AI-generated steps is a neat trick, but I often found it didn’t seem to understand what I was trying to achieve and I got caught in a bit of a loop for a while there trying to figure out what sort of task title would be ‘recognised’ enough for the AI checklist to work properly. Never actually figured that out. It’s cool, but not quite there yet. 

Very cool app, love how professional it feels, love LOVE the embedded notes app, but not really helpful for ADHD.

title: Don't get the lifetime subscription!
body:
I bought the lifetime subscription. Literally the day after I purchased it the app completely wiped itself, so I asked for a refund and it's been over a week and I haven't heard back from anyone! For the record, under Australian consumer laws I am entitled to a refund on any faulty product for up to a year after purchase! This company doesn't care about the people it supposedly wants to help! It only cares about taking your money!

Edit: just for the record, when I say I asked for a refund the email provided in the dev's response is exactly the method I used to contact the company (which as I said got no response)!

If the company was doing app maintenance, then I'm willing to give them another try (considering I still have almost a full year to still get a refund, and if the app ends up being helpful to me, then I want to use it), however there's no point providing me an email to contact for a refund when nobody from the company will respond to me through the proper communication methods!

Unless this company starts treating their customers better (regardless of whether I continue to stay with the app), my opinion remains the same as above! I shouldn't need to leave a public review to get recognition over a problem I'm having, and then be provided with what I expect is a completely useless email address, since that's how I was ignored in the first place!

Tiimo if you want people to support your company then treat ALL your customers with respect! Not just the customers who choose to stay with you! Afterall just because someone leaves, doesn't mean they aren't still willing to recommend you just because you might not have been the app they needed!

But I can promise you, considering my experiences here, I definitely won't be recommending you to anyone in the future! I don't feel like a respected and valued customer, I feel like I've been ignored and placated purely for the sake of your reputation, and NOT for the sake of you wanting to support your customers!

If you respect and support your customers, you'll make more money in the long run! That's just common sense!

title: Almost 5 stars
body:

Some suggestions. 

Editing event time is tricky. I change the finish time and it will alter the duration. This needs to be quicker. 

I have trouble estimating and planning out time over several days. It would be great to have projects with an estimated time and then as you schedule them out it adds up how much time you’ve allocated. That way I would be able to see if I have allocated enough time. 

Another suggestion would be grouping by categories or projects and then having some weekly stats. Eg to see how much time and percentage I have spent on leisure, work, fitness, down time each week. For example I have trouble planning out my week to fit in enough rest time, it would be great to be able to see that I planned out 4 hours or 5% down time this week but only got in 3 hours.

title: Life changing assistive technology
body:
Tiimo has been a central tool in my life for almost 2 years now. Having limited fine motor skills mean that paper planners aren’t an option for me, so executive dysfunction and my need for planning/routine was very difficult to meet previously. 

Being from Australia, currency conversion rates limit my access to neurodivergent-targeted assistive technology because it is often designed overseas. Considering how helpful Tiimo has been, I think it is excellent value for money. 

I was initially hesitant to commit to the subscription because I don’t generally use paid apps, and seeing reports of glitches and bugs furthered my wariness. I am so glad I ‘took a chance’ in this situation though, as Tiimo exceeded my expectations and has supported me through many major routine changes. It is a life changing piece of assistive technology in my life as an autistic+adhd young person.

I look forward to seeing how Tiimo develops in the future.

I have found an alternative app which is not quite as advanced but much less glitchy.

The Tiimo team have responded and none of that information they mentioned was communicated to me at the time. As someone with ADHD each glitch was a significant distraction, and the amount of mental effort it takes me to provide the feedback I did is quite high. Given neurological diverse people are your primary consumer it is super important to make sure people feel seen and heard.

Finally get it set up, only to realise days later that I’m not getting notified. Nothing in my notifications history. I’ve got it all set in app and on phone to do them, but it just stops after a few days. App is still running in background. 

This keeps happening. Sometimes closing and reopening the app fixes it. Sometimes changing something fixes it. It shouldn’t be happening to begin with. I don’t have the spoons. 

I need those prompts but they just don’t happen with any reliability. 

This app would only work for me if I didn’t have ADHD.

I would love to see it expanded more abd to be able to more easily add things into my premodern routines like if I know I need to do something extra one morning so I don’t have to manually change the start and end time of each event and also being able to edit your routines. For instance if you estimated when you started using an app a task would take you 30 minutes but it takes you 15. 
It would be great to be able to incorporate into the app a way of having daily task lists that you can move remaining daily tasks (like house hold cleaning) to the next day and have them repeated at specific frequencies.
Personally I love being able to have icons for each event so I have a visual cue, as well as the written task. For me this makes it easier in particular with how I have scheduled in taking my garbage, recycling and garden waste bins. Personally I put the colour of the bin lids as the icon and that works well for me. 🔴🟡🟢
As someone with ADHD it makes managing my routine a lot easier and i love that it links up with my watch so that I can focus on my routine more without getting distracted by my phone.
I am very keen to see the app develop more and be able to help more people.

title: Glasses for Time Blindness
body:
To get the most out of this app you need to understand the problem it’s solving. If you suffer with this problem, you’ll be more than happy to pay the subscription! (I think this is the reason for the poor ratings on this brilliant app).

If you have time blindness (look it up 🤓) + think more visually, and desperately want order in your life, this app is likely the answer.✅

People I see only occasionally have commented on how relaxed I seem 🏝. They all think I’m on holiday but it’s the result of not constantly chewing up all of my energy trying to keep an eye on my diary/calendar/clock, trying not to forget silly things like taking lunch to work (and still failing then stressing about it) and then being too exhausted to DO anything. 💤

I’ve tried SO many organisational systems 🗂 over the years and my inability to keep them going has left me feeling a bit lower each time. Using those tools only was like being taught how to focus on things by someone with 20/20 vision while everything is just blurry to me. Now that I have glasses (Tiimo) 👓 some of those systems may actually be useful! 

THANK YOU Tiimo team! 🍻

P.S. I’m normally too lazy/disorganised/in energy-conservation-mode to write these but made the effort this time because if all I have to do to help someone else in my situation get the results I have is write this then that’s a massive result to energy ratio and worth the trouble.

title: Could be better
body:
I fist intended to use this app for my daily routines & get things a bit more organized. However after many days using Tiimo I am seeing several issues in the way notifications & automations are done.

None of my notifications are working although they all have been approved. I am a Morning Routine which doesn’t display on my screen although I specified the time frame for it. 

Really nice widgets and Live Activity thing but I was expecting something automatic that would have started at the moment I wanted. Instead, I need to open the app every morning to make it work. Sometimes when I open it, Tiimo doesn’t show any Routine starting- I have to close the app, reopen it or sometimes I need to edit my Routine so it appears as “being tracked”. I don’t like this.

Another big issue I face is the connectivity with my Apple Watch. When I have an ongoing Routine and want to open in on my Watch, 8 times out of 10 I see a screen saying that I don’t have anything running. When I refresh / resync through the Watch app, it shows a Routine I can’t even update in real time. E.g this morning I wanted to complete the 2 first steps of it from my Watch but didn’t work, I wasn’t able to select the task although the screen clearly shows that it could be possible this way. 

Great design & stuff but not optimized yet.

title: Estaria aplaudindo de pé, se fosse possível
body:
Gente, que doideira! É literalmente tudo que eu procurava num aplicativo de organização. Design bonito, ferramentas úteis, bom funcionamento... além de ser totalmente liderado por mulheres, pelo que entendi. Simplesmente admirável. Percebi apenas alguns bugs ao tentar adicionar tarefas repetitivas em dias específicos, mas isso ocorreu uma ou duas vezes e não foi algo que me incomodasse de fato (nem algo que eu não conseguisse resolver sozinha). Então, tudo limpo.

Antes, eu usava o próprio bloco de notas do iPhone para me organizar. Acontece que ter um espaço reservado exclusivamente para as funções do Tiimo é, para mim, inegociável. Por isso, estou muito feliz por tê-lo encontrado, principalmente porque sou uma jovem adulta diagnosticada com autismo — não é todo dia que acho bons programas focados em auxiliar principalmente pessoas neurodivergentes. ❤️

Ressalto que estou utilizando o plano mensal pago porque preciso visualizar as tarefas no meu notebook, ou seja, pelo Tiimo for Web. Infelizmente, meu dinheiro está curto, mas gostaria de atualizar meu plano para o anual. Talvez em breve! Agora, o meu sonho é que um aplicativo oficial seja lançado para Windows, rs.

Enfim! Parabéns a toda a equipe envolvida no desenvolvimento do programa! Que vocês prosperem muito. Abraços do Brasil. 🇧🇷🥰

title: It’s promising, but not quite there yet
body:
Overall, the app concept is great, I love the clean interface, cute designs, the way it breaks tasks down by time, and the to-do list reminders.

That said, there are a few points worth addressing:

1. The desktop and mobile versions don't sync reliably. When I make edits to events, changes sometimes fail to save with no error message or loading indicator to explain what's happening. There's a lot of lag when editing or setting up calendar events.

2. The calendar view on desktop also has an alignment issue. Events scheduled close together appear misaligned, stacking left and right inconsistently.

3. As for the AI feature, I honestly don't use it. It feels underdeveloped, more like a placeholder than a functional tool. It struggles to interpret prompts correctly and rarely generates tasks as expected. I'd rather see that effort invested in core product functionality like the calendar setup experience.

For an iPhone App of the Year, I'd expect it to be more polished. With some focused improvements it could live up to that title. I hope to see meaningful updates that make it worth renewing my subscription.

title: 10/10 - O app pra Organização & Produtividade.
body:
Esse app é pra quem:
• tem dificuldade em organizar o dia dentro do tempo que tem;
• não consegue estimar o tempo de execução de cada tarefa;
• perde a concentração e se vê fazendo algo que não deveria.

O app é extremamente completo. 
Concentra todos os calendários e lembretes necessários a você, e ainda tem uma sessão de gestão de backlog. Todos esses itens culminam numa página de agenda, que te mostra o que foi planejado pro dia e ainda te conta se as atividades estão dentro do previsto por você.

Ele ainda conta com um timer de foco, que te ajuda a entender quanto tempo falta, focar na tarefa e até compreender se as estimativas que você dá estão sendo exequíveis.

Claro, sem esquecer que de acordo com o nome dado a tarefa que precisa ser feito, ele ainda te ajuda e dividir em itens menores tá facilitar e direcionar a execução, criando subtarefas através de IA acoplada.

title: Unfortunately, not ADHD friendly
body:
I’m just letting this warning here because it was nowhere to be found before I purchased the app: they REMOVED THE “ROUTINE” FUNCTION in some update, despite promoting this feature in all of their communications. That said, this really doesn’t matter AS MUCH, since you can still create one activity called, let’s say… “Morning Routine” and have subtasks on it.

But as an ADHDer myself, this app has 2 flaws that I simply cannot understand, even more on an app that is made by and for us neurodivergents: 1) it “punishes” you if you are late for any activity 2) it does not allow to enter activities with a due date+time, but without a defined duration. Let me explain:

1)
ALL activities have an individual and automatic timer, that starts at the due date/time an it is great to be able to see the activity and the time passing by in real time WHEN YOU CAN MAKE IT ON TIME. Because if you, for some reason are late, you CANNOT STOP IT, or even edit it. Only pause it. Also, if you accidentally tap on the “play” button right above an activity, you cannot undo it. For both cases (activity already started or accidentally tap on “play” button), you have to delete the activity and re-insert it!

Let me give an example: I had a swimming class today on my Google Calendar at 10AM but the teacher couldn’t make it and just told me after 10AM. Tiimo has an integration with GC, so it imported the event, but right at 10pm the timer started to roll until 11am, automatically! You cannot edit ANY event, the imported and/or the ones we create originally in app, AFTER it starts.

I wrote an email about all I’m writing here, and they’ve confirmed: I have to DELETE the activity and re-insert it again, with the new date/time. And if the activity was imported from GC, I have to go out of the app, go to Google Calendar, delete and re-enter the event with the new date+time. That’s more time wasting and more opportunities to make mistakes and forget things…

2)
Another big flaw for me is that we cannot create activities/events without a defined duration. Let’s say I want to wash my dishes at 2PM, but I don’t know how much time it takes yet. We all know “time blindness” is a struggle for us with ADHD and Autism! But in this app, instead, I have to create an activity on the day I want and leave it as “any time of the day” option, and remember that I need to do it by 2PM myself. That’s right, a planning app in which you have to use your own memory (and we all know how bad our memories are, that’s why we look for apps in the first place)…

They give us another workaround, that is to create the “washing dishes” task with an approximate duration and DURING THE ACTIVITY, keep tapping the “+” icon to add more minutes. With my hands wet?! And if I was on my swimming class and it was longer than it usually is? I have to leave the pool running and go to the app to add more time before the class ends?

How frustrating it is, to set an arbitrary time for something, like “editing a video”, and have to pause the activity itself to get the phone and keep adding minutes? How distracting and disappointing it is?

So, basically, I need to pay for this app and for another one like Toggl to first track the time I take to do every single activity in my life and then use Tiimo. That doesn’t make sense.

And another consequence of this, is that I cannot have on the same app, my tasks/activities and basic reminders, like someone’s birthday or holiday! If you import a “moon phase” or any calendar I just mentioned to Tiimo that is just an reminder for the day (and not a task per se), you have to set a timing duration or it will be together with the “anytime” tasks during the day.

I just don’t understand… so now I have to pay for Tiimo, Toggl and have to leave the app and enter on my Calendar app to see “all day” events that aren’t tasks, like “credit card due date”, or “Easter”. That’s the perfect recipe for failure as someone who struggles with focus and attention!

_

So, to summarize, on Tiimo, I have the following results by the end of my day:

• A swimming lesson that I supposedly did, but in reality didn’t;

• A pile of dishes in the sink, that I now have to wash in the evening when I am out of energy and tired, because I couldn’t guess the duration, so the task went to the “anytime” tab, that was closed to avoid distractions from the main ones;

• A full afternoon supposedly without any activity,  because I needed to use another app to track the time I took to edit a video, so that I can add it more accurately on Tiimo the next time;

• Oh, and I forgot to call my friend on her birthday, because I couldn’t add this event on Tiimo without a task attached to it and didn’t entered my Calendar app today 

_
I know the creator’s intentions are good, so I don’t plan on lashing out here. I really have tried the workarounds, but all I did was waste my money and patience. I’ll be testing Tick-Tick now, since they have all the functions mentioned, a minimalist layout and widgets way more useful!

title: Great for poor executive functions!
body:
I love this app so much! As a person with ADHD I need to have timed routines so I can do things without feeling overwhelmed, and the visual aspect of this app is so helpful! Besides, I love the awareness and research by the developers ❤️. The only reason I don’t give it 5 starts is because I’m missing some flexibility. 

Suggestions:

I’d love it if routines stayed as a unit rather than becoming individual when you drag them into the calendar, so by changing it in the folder you change all of them, as well as automatically rearranging the times when you change their order. It would also be great if there were a “start now” option and “snoozing” habits, pushing the whole routine forward. 

Im so grateful for this initiative and hope to see it continue to grow. I’m in it for the long run!

title: Manipulative tactics
body: They target people with ADHD, a condition known to impact impulse control, forgetfulness, and attention to detail. And they use manipulative ux design practices to take advantage of that. Before I've even had a chance to experience the app, there is a prompt to pay for premium, and of course the annual plan is selected by default. You know, the more expensive option that you're also conveniently most likely to forget about. And of course the only way to get the free trial is the annual plan. If you're not familiar with this manipulation tactic, you might not notice that you can just use the free version of the app by pressing the 'x' in the corner. (I have been tricked by this in the past so I don't think it's unreasonable to call it manipulative design for people with adhd). Not to mention the "one-time only offer" for 50% off an annual plan! That again, is before I have even had a chance to try the app. Terrible first impression.

title: Felt very exploitative. Instant delete.
body:
Before I could even see the app, I was shown a subscription screen. I tapped the X because I wanted to explore the product before paying. Instead of taking me to the app, it presented another sales screen stating: “This offer only appears once. Grab 40% off before it’s gone.”

I found this use of artificial urgency very exploitative. It pressures users to make an immediate purchasing decision before they can evaluate what they are buying. This is particularly troubling in an ADHD-focused app, since ADHD can involve impulsivity and difficulty making decisions under pressure.

The very next screen prompted me to rate the app, although I still had not seen or used it. That screen also advertised “Over 30,000 five-star reviews.” Requesting ratings before users have experienced the product undermines their credibility and makes me question how meaningful those reviews are.

An app claiming to support people with ADHD should hold itself to a much higher ethical standard. I deleted it immediately.

title: Too confusing to be useful
body:
I really wanted to like this app, especially since it’s marketed toward people with ADHD, but my experience has been frustrating.

The biggest issue is performance. Even on desktop, the app lags a lot, which makes it harder to stay focused instead of helping.

More importantly, the structure is confusing. There are multiple overlapping features like to-do lists, daily lists, schedules, and options to create additional lists. Instead of simplifying planning, it adds layers that feel overwhelming.

The AI features also don’t seem reliable. It sometimes creates duplicate categories instead of recognizing ones that already exist, which just adds more clutter.

title: My preferred app to stay on track with tasks and routines

I struggle with staying consistent and crossing things off my todo list and this app has really helped. 

The gamification — like the countdown timer and streamer when you complete a task — makes it really motivating and is very satisfying. 

I love that the UI is simple, full of useful demos and the widgets and calendar integrations keep everything in one place. 

Finally, I appreciate that the app was created by neurodivergent founders who understand firsthand some of the struggles neurodivergent users experience. 

My only complaint is that sometimes it can be buggy across devices — sometimes tasks don’t sync and the app freezes.

title: Heading in the wrong direction
body:
I’m using Tiimo begrudgingly and out of desperation. 

On one hand, it’s the only app I’ve managed to find that offers the niche functions I need: task management, time blocking, live activities and Apple Watch complications, and focus timers that automatically start at scheduled times. It allows me to plan my day in advance and reduce the friction of having to make in-the-moment decisions the following day, which is a big help for folks with ADHD. I can easily see what I should be doing at any given moment and how long I have left to do it. So yeah—kudos to making my days a bit easier.

On the other hand, the Tiimo team seems to be going in a direction that many users, myself included, don’t actually want—any amount of online research will reveal similar sentiments.

1. It’s clear that they’re trying to force users to use their AI assistant. From any tab in the app (including the focus timer), the purple assistant icon stares at you, begging to be clicked. On top of the icon, you’ll sometimes see a banner in the Today tab when you open the app, prompting you to plan your day with the assistant. I don’t doubt that it might be useful for some users, but why not provide the option to hide/toggle it off or at least put it in its own tab? The extra UI clutter for a feature that should be discretionary and the fact that the team is so heavy-handed with their promotion of it isn’t very ADHD-friendly. 

2. The ability to create and save custom routines is unclear. From the Today view, you have the option to explore routines from your recent tasks (those with sub-task) or select one from a library of premade routines. However, there’s no guidance about what a routine actually is in the context of the app and how to actually create one in a way that’s modular and intuitive. Your best bet is creating a to-do item with sub-tasks and then having it repeat, choosing a preset, or asking the chat assistant to help you.

3. Their website (not the web app) seems to bombard you with popups to subscribe to Pro each time you navigate to a new page. Being a paid subscriber who sometimes wants to just browse their resource or product pages, the popups are already quite irritating. But for a potential user looking to spend money and commit to a new app, the frequent interruptions are pushy and distracting—two things that set off alarm bells for someone with ADHD.

I really want to like Tiimo and use it long-term, which is why I put all this effort into typing up my feedback in the first place. I can largely ignore or overlook most of the issues I have with the app, and I believe the Tiimo team generally does care about supporting people with ADHD. 

But the app’s lack of flexibility and choice when it comes to their AI tool is a red flag for me—it points to a possible business-driven desire to be competitive in the AI space which, at least in my case, comes at the expense of user agency, needs, and preferences. I’ll likely stick with Tiimo until something better comes along, but I’m pessimistic about the direction the app’s development will take.

title: Close but not there yet
body:
There’s a big opportunity in the task management space: to leverage magic (AI) to help organize and de-clutter our busy lives. 

There’s a ton of “dumb” to-do list apps out there. Some have tried to grab the opportunity (Motion is one) but no one has succeeded. The main reason is that managing the app ends up feeling like work by itself. 

I had high hopes with Tiimo. On the surface it offers it all: beautiful UI, thoughtful UX, and an assistant that is suppose to auto-magically help you manage your list. 

The problem is that it doesn’t do that, so the whole promise falls apart. The AI-assistant is simply not good enough and so Tiimo ends up being just another to-do list to manage. I found it too frustrating to use. The assistant in Motion, despite its other flaws, did do something well: it gives ppl what they want: super simple and a zero-effort way to make sense of what to do next.

If Tiimo can greatly improve the assistant and offer us a magical “schedule my whole week” button…and does it intelligently, I would use the app all the time. I hope future updates improve this as I really believe it is trying to tackle a real and meaningful problem.

The design choice signals a push toward using the chatbot, but it performs poorly. It slows down basic actions, requires far more time than manual entry, and adds no value for simple tasks. Meanwhile, the actual “add task” button is undersized, low-contrast, and difficult to access. For these reasons, I do not intend to continue beyond the trial period.

title: Daily user for years until the latest update…
body: I was a loyal, daily user of this app for many years on a paid subscription until their most recent overhaul to how routines work. They also implied that if you didn’t update the app, this change wouldn’t affect you. I heavily relied on the time-based aspect for large routines (e.g. a morning routine) which was fantastic when used with my Apple watch. It was a massive game changer in terms of not losing track of time or tasks that needed to be done in a time crunch as a neurodivergent person. Their newest forced update to routines is frankly horrible, they’ve turned robust routines with timed aspects and notifications into a checklist - making this no better than writing down a list. I had a busy, time-sensitive morning routine all planned out for today and woke up to see it had turned into a checklist in the app, which was extremely jarring to say the least. I used to love this app but considering its geared toward neurodivergent folks, they sure do love to make massive design overhauls or change the entire system constantly which is a little ironic considering many neurodivergent people struggle with change and/or rely on routine heavily. Because of this latest update it looks like I’ll be cancelling my subscription after nearly 5 years, and going back to an old fashioned checklist. RIP to what was once the best planning app I’d ever used.

title: Inclusive Intentions, But Falls Short for Visually Impaired Users
body:
I was initially excited about the potential of the Tiimo app, hoping it would assist me, a neurodiverse individual, in organizing my day and breaking down tasks. However, my experience was hindered by the app's lack of accessibility for visually impaired users.

Despite the developers' emphasis on intersectionality, the app falls short in catering to the needs of individuals with visual impairments. The absence of compatibility with Apple's built-in accessibility features for the blind, such as font size adjustments, makes the app unusable for those who rely on these features.

While the developers advocate for intersectionality, they seem to overlook the reality that many individuals face multiple disabilities, both physical and neurodiverse. The visually appealing design of the app contrasts sharply with its inaccessibility to visually impaired users, reinforcing the exclusionary nature of technology for those with diverse disabilities.

As someone who is Non-Binary, Mad, Neurodiverse, Chronically Ill and Visually Impaired, I find it disappointing that an app claiming to champion intersectionality neglects a significant portion of its potential user base. The review serves as a call to action for developers to align their words with meaningful steps towards inclusivity for ALL. 

Anybody who may be looking for an app like Tiimo that is accessible to those who are Low Vision or Blind, check out the Structured app. From the start, their app has been accessible to those most marginalized by inaccessible technology. 

Do better.

title: Extremely Disappointing -an autistic habit & schedule app explorer
body:
I had high hopes due to it being marketed towards people like me (Autism, ADHD, and more) and I’m now deleting it more disappointed than i expected. This app has been much more difficult to use as an auDHD person than others i’ve tried. It absolutely has potential, but its currently too flawed, disorganized, complex, visually unappealing to be worth using imo.

1. My Day and Library don’t seem to be synced, in that deleting something in one doesn’t delete it in the other, so theres no actual way to see a list of all of your routines & activities.

2. Editing an activity in the Library will create a duplicate in both the library and the day planner which you have to individually delete.

3. Editing a routine in My Day will create a duplicate in My Day that doesn’t show up in the routine Library.

4. There’s no separation between repeating activities/routines and one time activities/routines in the Library, so activities like “feed the cat” or “do laundry” will be mixed in with “watch star wars” or “stitch hole in jeans” from 3 months ago. It’s more of a history tab than a library.

5. Activities and Routines take up an unnecessary amount of space in My Day to the point where you can only see maybe 2 on your screen at once. Routines particularly have huge chunks of unnecessary empty space both when theyre expanded and when theyre collapsed.

6. No transition between activities & routines in My Day. Its just block after block. An example of good visual transitions between events can be found in an app called Structured, which will remain my primary app despite having less features.

7. You can only ever see the plan for one day at a time, ie theres no way to get a glance at the coming week (i expected this to appear in the top bar of the My Day page when i added tasks but it didn't)

8. Glitches. A lot.

and more, but I can’t remember them. Bye!

title: The idea is there, but not executed well…
body:
The idea of this app is great, especially for someone with adhd, however there are some major flaws that make it frustrating to use. Honestly unless they fix the issues, it’s not worth using. 

It’s great for planning your day and setting reminders for tasks. I often find it hard to manage my time and don’t realize how long specific tasks take. The app was great to help me plan my mornings to ensure I have enough time to get everything done before work. However, if you set a time for a task, the app automatically checks the task off even if you haven’t completed and won’t let you uncheck it if it’s in a routine, so then I’m scrambling trying to fix it, getting flustered, ultimately making my adhd worse. 

Solution: only allow tasks to be checked off manually once user actually completes them. If the task takes longer than intended, let it go into overtime. We are not robots and it is normal to run a few minutes or seconds behind…

author: dhshja akd

title: Thank you from the bottom of my heart ❤️
body:
This app helped me so much in such a short period of time! It made me « see » time. I have never been able to incorporate time into my perception of the world and organize myself with it. In my mind, I have all the time in the world or none at all at the same time. 

The day after setting up my routines and activities, I arrived at work 20 minutes in advance and I didn’t have to run to get there! Just casually walk! It NEVER happens!

It was amazing to feel the weight of the stress I felt since I was little finally being lift off of my shoulders.

Using it made me able to do the amount of tasks I usually do in three weeks, in only three days! It’s amazing! It really keeps me focus and motivated and it is really satisfying to check the tasks that are done. I still can’t estimate the time it will take me to do a series of tasks, but I can with one and the app calculates the total of them together so I can organize myself to finish at the right time and not be late.

I discovered that I probably have ADD (not sure for the « H ») with an article on their blog. Now, I can go and get tools to improve my life with that information.

It’s cliché, but this app changed my life in the best way possible as I am struggling to organize myself starting a business to teach gardening while working 40h/week.

It is a great tool, and the people behind it do it with passion and it shows. I was won over by their ethics when I read that they didn’t put adds in for a free version because it defied the purpose of the app and that they are trying to keep it as low of a price as possible so that more people can use it while they can provide for themselves as a company. I applaud this!

Please continue your great work! It is trully helpful.

Thank you! Thank you! Thank you!

title: Almost perfect although a couple of bugs/suggestions
body:
As a person with ADHD I actually really like this app. It helps me keep track of the tasks that absolutely need to be done each day. That is what I use it for. There are a couple of things that I wish could be included in this app or adjusted. 

For one I would like there to be an Apple Watch complication that didn’t involve me having to open the app on Apple Watch. Even just the emoticon or title of your next task on your watch screen all the time would be super helpful. I personally need reminders to start these things because I’m constantly thinking of other things and incredibly forgetful so having it front and centre every time I looked at my watch would be super helpful. 

Also I’ve had issues where tasks that don’t have specific start times do not show up on the iOS widget until you actually start them. I would like it just to show me the tasks that I have to do whether they have a specified start time or not. The majority of my day the widget says well done even though I have not completed the tasks that I have set for that day. It would also be nice to have an option of the smaller square widget and not just the medium one. 

Other than that it’s a great app and I totally recommend it.

title: Why?
body:
I started using Tiimo as soon as I was diagnosed with Asperger's and ADHD, and it was truly a lifesaver. It was simple, intuitive, and non-overwhelming—it actually motivated me to plan and follow my day. I used it for about two years and loved it. 

However, after this recent update, I’ve really struggled to use it. They changed the font, the way tasks are added, and how things are displayed. While I understand they’ve added many new features that might be helpful to others, they seem to have completely overlooked the user experience. 

This is an app specifically designed for people who dislike sudden changes or struggle with complex steps, yet this update introduced so many new elements, steps, and design changes. It’s no longer a helpful tool for me; instead, it has become a source of frustration. Unfortunately, I won’t be renewing my subscription.

title: Wundervolle App mit Potential für noch mehr Funktionen
body:
Tiimo hilft mir wirklich, meinen Tag zu strukturieren. Das Design ist ruhig und übersichtlich, und die visuelle Planung mit Dauer und Symbolen gefällt mir sehr. Ich nutze die App sogar in Workshops, in denen ich Menschen mit Beeinträchtigung davon erzähle und ihnen die App empfehle - alle sind begeistert. 

Ein Punkt stört mich und viele Workshop-Teilnehmende allerdings noch: Meine Apple-Erinnerungen und -Kalender werden zwar angezeigt, aber die Synchronisierung funktioniert nur in eine Richtung. Wenn ich in Tiimo eine Aufgabe anlege, etwa „XY“ im Tab „shopping“, kann ich als Liste nur „To-dos“ wählen. Die Aufgabe landet dann in Tiimos Standardliste und nicht in meiner One-Way synchronisierten Apple-Liste. Dasselbe gilt für Kalendereinträge. 

Ich wünsche mir eine echte Zwei-Wege-Synchronisierung. Dann könnte ich Aufgaben und Kalendereinträge in meinen bestehenden Listen anlegen und bearbeiten, und alles wäre in beiden Apps auf demselben Stand. Das wäre für mich das perfekte Update. Danke für die tolle Arbeit!

Daneben wäre es noch optimal, wenn bei Einträgen die Beschreibungen schon vorab sichtbar wären und nicht erst, wenn man auf „Bearbeiten“ klickt. 

Ich habe große Hoffnung, dass euer tolles Team diese Features einbauen kann, weil sie super hilfreich sind.

title: Beautiful design, but frustrating to use
body:
I’ve had a Tiimo subscription for two years, and I genuinely like the design and visual approach of the app. Unfortunately, I keep running into the same problem: there’s so much friction involved in creating, editing, and rescheduling tasks that I eventually stop using it after a few weeks.

Ironically, for me, it’s one of the least ADHD-friendly planners I’ve tried. A planner should reduce the mental effort required to organize my day, not become another task I have to manage.

I’ve also given the AI assistant several chances, but so far it’s been more of a waste of time than a helpful feature. For example, I gave it a simple instruction to schedule my work shifts for next week, from 16:00 to midnight, with Tuesday and Thursday off. It initially scheduled me for all seven days, and I had to repeatedly clarify the instructions and specify exact dates to prevent it from changing other weeks.

By the time the AI finally understands what I want, I’ve spent more time explaining and correcting it than it would have taken to enter everything manually.

I really want to love Tiimo because the visual design is excellent. But the functionality needs to be much more intuitive, flexible, and reliable. For an ADHD planner, reducing friction should be the number one priority.

title: Good but won’t use like this
body:
I really like the idea behind Tiimo and I can see how helpful it can be, especially for people with ADHD and time blindness. The visual planning, reminders, and focus timer are great concepts.

However, there are a few things that would make the app much more useful for me:

First, I would love better time tracking. It would be amazing if Tiimo could learn from my habits and show things like: “You usually need 10 minutes longer for this type of task” or give average completion times after doing the same task multiple times. Right now, I often don’t know how long things actually take me, which is exactly what I’m trying to improve.

Second, the focus timer needs a stronger end notification. If I don’t use the focus music, I often don’t notice when the timer ends. For people with ADHD, a subtle ending is not always enough because we may not notice the transition. A clearer alarm sound or customizable end-of-timer notification would make this feature much more effective.

I also wish the AI features were more advanced. At the moment, it doesn’t really feel like the AI understands my tasks, helps me break them down, or supports me in organizing them in a meaningful way.

Another thing I struggle with is having to put every task directly into my calendar. I don’t like filling my calendar with things that aren’t actual appointments. I would prefer having a flexible to-do list without fixed times, where I can choose tasks depending on my energy and available time. However, I would still like to see afterwards at what time I actually completed each task and how long it took me. When I fall behind or something takes longer than expected, my whole schedule currently feels ruined, which is stressful and not very different from just adding tasks to a free calendar app.

I think Tiimo has a lot of potential, but adding flexible task management, better time insights, stronger AI support, and improved timer notifications would make it a much more powerful tool.

title: Life changing
body:

The app is super fun and for me personally an absolute gamechanger. 

What I don’t like:
- I still get reminders about discount codes although I purchased the pro version

- there could be more emojis for tasks

- when I move a task that has a reminder set it will still start ringing at the initial time. That is very annoying (your phone will just start ringing out of nowhere) and preventing this makes it more time consuming to move said tasks. 

But all in all the best planning app I’ve ever come across. Finally I don’t have to buy notebook after notebook that won’t work anyways.

title: Tolle Ideen, schlechte Umsetzung
body:
Ich durfte Tiimo nun für ein paar Tage kostenfrei probieren. Im Vergleich mit  anderen Tages-Planungs-App‘s hat Tiimo meiner Meinung nach den besten Ansatz. 
Leider ist die technische Umsetzung aktuell so fehlerhaft, dass eine langfristige Nutzung für mich aktuell nicht in Frage kommt. Dazu gehören Punkte wie eine KI, die in meiner Sprache antwortet,  importierte Erinnerungen, die sich nicht bei Import vervielfachen (eigentlich sollten diese Synchronisiert werden, nicht nur importiert), Kalender die korrekt synchronisiert werden (inklusive Wegzeit) und eine Zeitleiste, die ich wirklich per Drag and Drop umstrukturieren kann (ohne dass meine Aufgaben mit einer Startzeit von 00:00 Uhr versehen werden). 
Meiner Meinung nach ist es sehr schade, dass all diese technischen Probleme diese App unbrauchbar machen. Von den Ideen her, mit dem Aufgaben Timer, der lockeren Tagesunterteilung Ohne feste Zeiten und vielen anderen Dingen, ist es nämlich die von vielversprechendste App die ich bisher getestet hab. 
PS: Bitte antwortet nur, wenn Ihr etwas produktives zu sagen habt. Ich benötige keine Antwort, wenn es nur die Standard Antwort von einem Bot ist, der hofft das ich in Zukunft 5 Sterne geben werde.

title: Einfach nur klasse! :)
body:
Ich habe jetzt schon mehrere Planerapps ausprobiert und diese hier ist mit Abstand die beste.
Mir gefällt, dass man ein Abo abschließen kann aber es auch ohne geht und trotzdem keine Werbung oder große Einschränkungen gibt. Ich finde das Layout sehr ansprechend und ich mag es sehr das man seine Aufgaben nicht nur nach Uhrzeit ordnen kann sondern auch nach anderen Kriterien, wie Morgens, etc. 
Was ich auch sehr ansprechend finde: die Fokusfunktion. Man kann die Aufgabe starten und z.B. anfangen aufzuräumen und hat auch nicht das Bedürfnis an sein Handy zu gehen und sieht auch wie lange man schon beispielsweise gelernt hat. 
Ebenfalls mag ich, dass man seine To Do‘s unabhängig vom Tag priorisieren kann nach Hoch, Mittel und Niedrig. 
Vielen Dank für diese tolle App!

Allerdings vermisse ich einige Funktionen:
1) mehrere Aufgaben auswählen und verschieben (nur möglich bei der abendlichen Zusammenfassung?!)
2) verschieben von täglichen Aufgaben in die ToDo’s nicht möglich
3) die terminierten Aufgaben würde ich gerne über den „jederzeit“-Aufgaben in der täglichen Übersicht sehen. Es gibt leider keine Anpassungsmöglichkeit
……
Fazit: Hübsch - jedoch unausgereift. Der Abopreis nicht berechtigt, die Funktionen gibt es in vielen kostenlosen Apps

title: Sehr hilfreich, aber mit Potenzial zur Verbesserung
body:
Ich habe angefangen tiimo zu benutzen, weil ich Schwierigkeiten habe Aufgaben zu priorisieren und meinen Alltag zu planen. Ich habe ADHS und tiimo hilft mir sehr dabei mich selbst zu managen. Ich habe auch einige andere Apps für To-Do-Listen und Zeitmanagement ausprobiert, jedoch war das Erscheinungsbild im Vergleich zu tiimo oft sehr steril und trotzdem nicht so übersichtlich und intuitiv nutzbar. Ich liebe die intuitive Bedienung der App. 
So sehr ich diese App mag , gibt es jedoch ein paar Kritikpunkte und ich wünsche mir diesbezüglich noch Verbesserungen in der App. 

1. Es wäre sehr praktisch wenn die App auch offline funktioniert. Wenn mal keine Verbindung zum Internet besteht, kann ich keine neuen Aufgaben hinzufügen und in der App planen. 
Ich wünsche mir eine Möglichkeit zur Offline-Nutzung mit anschließender Synchronisierung bei erneuter Verbindung zum Internet  
2. Die Option zum Anhängen von Bild-, Text- und Audio-Dateien wäre sehr praktisch 
3. Die Implementierung der Erinnerungen von iOS ist toll. 
Eine Implementierung der iOS Notizen wäre auch sinnvoll und hilfreich.


Liebes Team von tiimo, 
Ich nutze eure App jeden Tag und findet es toll Erinnerungen und Kalender in einer App vereint zu haben. 
Ich würde mich sehr freuen, wenn ihr euch meine Rezension zu Herzen nehmt und etwas davon umsetzen könnt. 

Liebe Grüße 🌝
author: Tobi537

title: Synchronisations- und Benachrichtigungsprobleme
body:
Ich habe das Jahresabo bestellt, weil mir die Zusammenführung von allen Themen sehr gut gefällt. Ich habe die To-dos da drin, Google und Apple Kalender, und kann eigene To-dos hinzu nehmen und den Tag planen. Das ist super. Aber bei der Synchronisierung von Widges zur Tiimo App und zu Google und Apple werden manche Einträge nicht mitgenommen. Das ist ein Gau und macht eine vernünftige Nutzung dieser App nahezu unmöglich. 
Update: Jetzt nervt er noch. Benachrichtigungen sind abgestellt, kommen dennoch. Auf der Watch gelöscht, Aufforderungen kommen dennoch. Ich muss mir das Handy schon einstellen können wie ich will. Das Abo ist gekündigt. Schade ums Geld.

title: Vorsicht beim Abo Abschluss! Geld rausgeschmissen..
body:
Eigentlich wollte ich die App nur mal testen und ihr eine Chance geben..
Leider geht das nicht ohne ein (Jahres!) Abo abzuschließen. OK- man kann ja innerhalb einer Woche kündigen, dachte ich.
Leider war auf meinem Apple Account nicht genug Guthaben als „Sicherheit“ für ein Jahresabo. Also bin ich zurück in die Aboauswahl und habe mich für ein 9 euro Monats Abo entschieden.
Leider habe ich erst viel zu spät bemerkt dass in einem Monats Abo keine Woche Testzeitraum inkludiert ist. Zum scheinbaren Glück erschien im Bezahl Prozess unten noch ein Button für den endgültigen Abschluss des Abos. Diesen vermied ich zu betätigen. Dennoch habe ich offenbar ein Monatsabo abgeschlossen!?!
Okay dachte ich und öffnete die App diese schien zunächst nicht zu wissen dass ich sie bezahlt hatte und die Funktionen waren nicht vollständig freigeschaltet. Nach einigem hin und her war die App dann doch irgendwie nutzbar.
Leider musste ich sehr schnell feststellen dass die App für mich völlig unübersichtlich ist. Ich habe überhaupt keine Ahnung wie sie zu bedienen ist beziehungsweise sehe absolut kein Mehrwert zur normalen Kalender und Aufgaben App von iOS. Zumal man an manchen Stellen aus der App einfach zur iOS Aufgaben Ansicht übergeben wird ohne dass die jeweils betreffende Aufgabe ausgewählt wäre. Ich habe keine Ahnung was mir das bringen soll. Insofern hätte ich die App beziehungsweise das Abo direkt gern widerrufen. Dazu fand ich allerdings keine Möglichkeit.
Sollte es noch eine Möglichkeit geben das Abo zu kündigen beziehungsweise den gezahlten Betrag zurückzuhalten wäre ich dafür sehr dankbar ansonsten muss ich sagen war es leider teures Lehrgeld für eine aus meiner Sicht sehr unübersichtliche und unausgereift App. Interessanterweise stellte ich im Nachhinein fest dass es offensichtlich bei dieser App sehr viele Abomodell gibt die unterschiedliche Gebühren nach sich ziehen und unbekannte Leistungsumfänge beinhalten. In dem Moment wo man die App allerdings installiert werden meiner Ansicht nach nur zwei Modelle angeboten und zwar nicht unbedingt die günstigsten. Auch das erscheint mir etwas undurchsichtig.

author: krokoschga

title: High potential but improvable
body:
What I really like about the app:

- the idea 
- the AI-functions! Amazing and really helpful for time blindness and planning 
- the inclusion of the visual part like how many hours left until the next task is due and the visual timer 
- created by neurodiverse folks
- continuous improvement 

What I think could be improved:

- Apple Watch App often doesnt match the other apps 
- visual structure - tasks for the whole day can be easily forgotten as you scroll over them , which can be difficult as with ADHD there often is a problem with „out of sight out of mind“
- could be more minimalistic as I feel I can not quite differentiate  important from not so important info 
- categorizing according to importance
- if you want to cross off subtasks it often doesn’t work quite well , instead of opening the subtasks it gets you directly to change the whole task, if you do not press the ideal spot. This can sometimes be frustrating and sometimes keeps me from opening the subtasks 
- sometimes the calendar sync doesn’t transfer dates, especially if they are planned to be for the whole day 
- I know why you decided to go against a weekly or monthly overview. In my opinion it would still be helpful, as it would allow to not forget long term tasks (ie exams, doctors appointments) for which longer prep can be necessary. I know you could create tasks to remind you beforehand. My experience in daily life is, that you sometimes just have time to write the important date in the calendar without being able to write down reminders or you simply forget to set the reminders, which is quite the problem with ADHD

I really look forward to see what the app is like in the future and I think it has great potential!

author: ojjjeola

title: Good idea, bad implementation
body:
I like the concept of having full routines instead of just tasks. Unfortunately, there is a new functionality breaking bug every few days. Yesterday, I paused a routine, but could not restart it anymore. I already stopped using the watch for the app because that constantly broke it (tasks would have negative duration and never finish etc). So today I thought I avoid the pause button and instead delete the routine and recreate it. Turns out the new bug of the day is that I can’t edit the routine anymore at all. There is no quality assurance process at all. Instead they randomly change and break things with every update. Not usable if you need consistency.

I now deleted it and regret all the time I lost trying to use this app.

title: Can’t tab out during registration
body:

Basically, the app is unusable.
