title: It's not a Planner. Makes me feel MORE disabled.
body:
Tiimo has some good stuff.  
I haven't used the app for months because I was so put off by the frustrating bugs when tried to add monthly bills.  

Today I realized that I really want to try to use an iPad/iPhone app for my primary calendar instead of a paper one...  and it seems that tiimo ios doesnt have a week or month view.  Only the desktop version has month view.  This doesn't make sense.  For an app that costs money and has SO MANY extra features, even courses... the absence of something so essential to planning makes me feel like I must not be human or have once again slipped into a dystopian universe.                       I can't confidently set daily goals in the morning or review and re-plan at the end of the day without seeing long term views!  Like how can anyone?  									I have a great visual memory, but apparently this app is made for you the majority who can memorize and visualize all your long term goals, tasks, and events/appointments to the point you don't need to view them when daily planning and working.  												 
September 24:    complete failure on first attempt to set up.
I just updated to ios 18.1 and it will NOT save items i set to repeat on a monthly date (such as bills).  I've tried multiple times and they keep resetting to "today / anytime"   It's be.  Truly bizarre.   

ALSO:  There NEEDS to be a place to view different tasks/ events as chronological lists.    

Even in the first days of Apple and Google calandars you can click and unclick which categories we want to see show up - so we can choose to view everything in a list or on a monthly or weekly calendar   or we can view different combinations of these subcategories :  
a. daily repeating / anytime tasks    
b. monthly tasks  
c.  one time tasks         
It's so MADDENING to see all these crandom events cluttering up my tasks from facebook or google, including acquatinance birthdays or community events I'm not interested in.   You can't click on them to make them go away!
Come on now.  This is basic planner type stuff!   If this doesn't get fixed in the next 3 days, I'm going to need a refund, because this app will be completely worthless to me.  I need something that can do all these things, otherwise I might as well just have a bunch of different free apps that only do parts of these things.

The symptoms of being born with ADHD caused a massive amount of abuse in my life, resulting in a lifelong physical disability that has sent me to the ER 19 times within the past 5 years. I wasn’t “allowed” to even get tested by doctors. The doctors dismissed me, my parents called it “YOUR MENTAL ILLNESS”, fired from jobs although I earned and paid for dual bachelors degrees … I also have a Masters degree. Currently, I have no job and have been living in my car for almost a year. My previous roommate screamed at me and chased me down the street saying I should have told her I have ADHD. Now, barely getting back up on my feet thanks to finally being diagnosed and educating myself to be able to talk about it instead of feeling shame. I’m not feeling my $42/yr for this ONE app having much, if any, benefit to climbing out of the mud pit ADHD has left me in despite my efforts and aptitude. Do better.

author: Jacob A Norris

title: Overall, I’m a FAN!
body:
UPDATED:
Tiimo developers seem to be continually listening and adjusting the app based on feedback, which is very much appreciated. The updates have made planning much easier, and my timers are now synched. SUPER happy that my page now immediately opens to the planning vs the learn section. I am OK with the routines being gone now since I find the suggestions for “self-care” even better because what is offered is great and I can easily customize. I am still hoping options for a palette come out but it’s fine. I am a fan of this app and will continue to pay for the learn portion, too. It’s always great to have resources to understand more about how brains work! 

PREVIOUS:

I am willing to invest in an app to keep myself on task and organized. While I didn’t want to pay right away, I got an offer (that would shortly expire) for 25% off so took the leap after playing with it for a day. I am already frustrated. If I schedule a task, like a meeting, but then the meeting runs over…that will affect the rest of my plans. This happened today. But once the Tiimo time starts, it’s VERY difficult to readjust the other tasks. I knew there (unfortunately) wasn’t an easy way to batch-shift all tasks to a new time (say, move them all 15 minutes), but I was willing to adjust each one. The problem is, again, once the timer starts. My only choices are to resume or pause the task. Pausing it makes it look gray as though I have completed it. Editing it does NOTHING, inexplicably. The only surefire way is to delete the task and start all over again—how is this effective for saving mental energy and time?

Also, it would be really helpful if there was a way to select colors and create our own palette that could be used consistently and easily. While there is a way to save colors, it’s clunky to get to them.

I also read that there is a way to create routines but either that’s gone now or it’s just not intuitive for me.

title: TERRIBLE UPDATE REMOVED ROUTINES
body:

Honestly DO NOT pay to subscribe to an app that deletes not only its best, core functionality that you can get for free come Google calendar and Tasks.

title: Beautiful Design, But Fails on Functionality
body:
Tiimo has a stunning interface and a calming aesthetic, but unfortunately, that’s not enough. The routines feature is completely missing, which is baffling given the app's purpose. Without routines or the ability to include subtasks with custom times, the app falls short of supporting those with executive functioning challenges — the very group it's marketed to help.
As it stands, Google Calendar combined with Google Tasks does a better job at planning and structure — and it’s free. Tiimo feels like a premium wrapper around features that are either missing or half-implemented. It’s a nice idea, but without the fundamentals, it doesn’t deliver where it matters most.

title: 🚀Life changing for neurodivergent people‼️
body:
Tiimo is for us, neurodivergent people; since trying it 2 months ago, the way my days go is different. I’m happier and more confident ; the level of executive functioning I’m able to muster + tasks I’m able to get done is remarkable in comparison to beforehand… and again, it’s done so much for my self esteem. Because I’ve always had so many ideas and goals but never can execute them due to my ADHD…d I’ve tried EVERY paper planner & planner app under the sun, and nothing works after the initial dopamine of a new system wears off… the tool becomes another task….. But Tiimo is so obviously designed by us and for us, neurodivergent friends! 

It not only is the first system to stick for me , but  it also actually helps me not only be more productive but have an overall higher QOL — thank you for finally making our people an app that’s a real TOOL — I feel like for the first time I can finally use my ADHD super powers to my advantage . 

The app features are great and unique (truly the timer…..a stroke of genius that could only be from a neurodivergent brain ) , but I also equally love the community sense from the app… ADHD makes follow-through so hard, and so many of us are so hard on ourselves and suffering in silence — this app’s got a built in neurodivergent community to help me be accountable. From the music live sessions to the courses on and designed for being productive within our neurodivergence make me feel supported ! I Can’t recommend this enough to everyone with ADHD — if you wanna know , finally, what it feels like to be productive consistently via a tool / system that’s implemented so easily , this is a must. The paid subscription is also so cheap …. Worth it!

body:
I really loved this app when I first got it almost a year ago! It was very intricate and encouraging to get things done, even with my ADHD symptoms. 

Now, I feel like it’s gotten a lot more bland and buggy. I don’t get consistent notifications for my scheduled tasks, and checking off items leaves them stuck in the list of I check them off too fast. 

I’m paying for the premium version of this app yearly, but now I’m considering not renewing because of how disappointing it has become. I hope the devs can get out back to what it was, or better!!

author: Getting real POed rn

title: Fantastic Planner and Use of AI
body: I’ve only ever written 3 reviews in my life and this is one of them. I have been looking for ages for an affordable planner app which does all of the following 1) has both task and time put into them 2) calendar that syncs to everything seamlessly (work, school, iOS etc) 3) graphics design that is done well, this app is extremely beautiful and intuitive and if you are confused there’s easily accessible tutorials. 4) A timer to help me focus on one task at a time. 5) Easy to work with and not childish(no pets or garden things) 6) Affordable let’s be honest 10 dollars is equivalent to a nice pen/note planner but that doesn’t compare with all this app can do + the ease of never losing it. I have to say to developers well done, there’s no competition in my eyes and I can’t wait to be impressed by your future improvements.

author: scary-dragon

title: Great idea, poor web app execution
body: I really loved the concept of this app and would love to find something that has these same unique features. However, I work best with native desktop apps (being on my phone is incredibly distracting), so I tried the web app. While it works, it does not have all the same features as the iPhone app (like “anytime” folder just isn’t there, so I can’t add something to ‘anytime’, nor schedule a task from ‘anytime’) and they just *do not* sync properly. I almost wish they didn’t provide the sync so it wasn’t so confusing. It does not handle multiple events well (I was making dinner and also working while the food was in the oven). And if a task takes longer than expected I can’t go back and change it or add more time? I wish that when a task ended instead of saying “great job!” it started counting UP to show you how much time you’re now OVER your predicted time allotment. I wanted to leave a review bc I really like this app, but it’s unusable for me the way it is, so I hope some great improvements are made (native desktop??) so it can be even better.

title: Pretty Good!
body:
Overall, this app is quite good for neurodivergents. It offers many useful features without cluttering the user interface or experience. The design of the focus timer can be a bit peculiar at first, especially if you schedule work for more than an hour with multiple subtasks. The visual countdown isn’t very intuitive until the last hour. While the UI design for the iPhone is satisfactory, the iPad version feels somewhat underwhelming—though this is just my preference, as I tend to be on my iPad more for work than my iPhone. I know there’s a web version available with more features, but it raises the question of why use that when there’s an iPad app. 

Overall, I enjoy this app, but I'm considering switching to another one with similar features that cost a little less annually and include AI capabilities, which I find helpful for breaking down tasks into smaller subtasks.
author: Digitalfigment

title: Broken hearted
body:
Like so many planner apps, Tiimo has joined fully with AI and stripped away all the beloved parts that made this application amazing. What’s been stripped away:
• Community offerings
• Learning webinars
• Body Doubling sessions
• Routines
• Music (Lofi channel was awesome)
• Daily reflection/check-in

I would pay the $96.00 if this incredible app wasn’t a total shell of its former self. It makes me sad (and resigned) because this was the first phone app I could use and not feel overwhelmed. I recommended Tiimo to everyone. Now I’m without a phone planner again. Way to go, AI! 🙄

title: Took away all the useful features
body:

They took away their best feature, claim to ‘care about their audience’ and refuse to add routines back in-spite of hundreds of complaints from users that they need that feature. 

What they started with was great! Routines! A visual timer! Great! Lots of icons! Great!

But the app is now over engineered with a bunch of nonsense (pages of ‘tips’ for managing your ADHD or ASD (distracting and adds clutter)), a mood tracker (tons of other apps do this better), music for some reason?? Body doubling?? (Another thing done better many other apps). 

I wish they would go back to the core of what this app was! A visual routine scheduler for ADHD/Autism.

body:

The ability to schedule a routing, just daily as needed and help with time management and planning was unmatched by nearly any other app. They’ve removed the beta app and, while consistently acknowledging suggestions from users on every other topic, strictly ignore the requests to bring back routine despite it being one of the  most popular suggestion/requests.

For now - use Routinly. It’s missing some features but functionality is far beyond Tiimo now that they’ve swapped to simple tasks.

title: Highly Disappointed
body: I was quite excited to try this app to help stay on task throughout the day and battle ADHD symptoms. But after using it for about a week, I couldn’t be more disappointed. It’s a fairly well-polished app and looks beautiful, but form seemed chosen over function. For example, there is no way to snooze a task or have it roll into the following day if it goes incomplete for the day; so I had to go backwards and reschedule all of the incomplete tasks for new dates. This was not ideal for someone with ADHD. It’s too easy to forget tasks as it is, and the app simply started a new day with a blank slate rather than addressing the ones that were incomplete from the day before. I couldn’t understand the lack of features so I tried the pro subscription. There was no free trial offered, but I took a risk to give the app more of a chance. The risk did not pay off, and now Apple is refusing to refund me for a year’s subscription after only using the app for less than a week. Tiimo also made the timer feature a prime function, but it was rather buggy and unreliable. Additionally, tasks that were scheduled for a time would automatically start a timer at that time whether I wanted it to or not. This didn’t make sense to me and I’d often felt rushed into a task that I was not ready for. It was like the app would punish you for being late to start something scheduled. I think Tiimo would work well for a lot of people, but not for me. And I don’t understand why I wasn’t given a free trial. Now I am out $41 for an app that I no longer use.

author: Funphone(:! 321

title: This App Changed My Life
body: I can’t express what Tiimo is to me as an app and the degree to which it has changed my life. I encourage every neurodivergent person I know to try it. I have struggled my entire life with time blindness and staying current with my self care routines. I am a person who desperately needs routines to function but has trouble maintaining them. I built my routines into the app and add them to my schedule daily and it helps me figure out more than any other tool I’ve tried how to carve out that time for myself. I also am able to create much more realistic goals for myself because it forces me to think about how much time things actually take. Setting realistic goals and not over scheduling myself has lead to a greater sense of accomplishment that in turn encourages me to accomplish more. I also have been more on time to things than I have ever been. I end every day with the review function and plan out the next day. It helps me so much with the paralysis I’ve always felt when deciding what to do and what is most important to prioritize. Also, this app is created by the most incredible team. They are not just pumping this app out here- they legitimately deeply care about their mission to create a productivity app for neurodivergent people. I heard about an upcoming feature change that I used heavily and was concerned. I sent them a loooong email not expecting to hear back. They not only responded but helped me to understand the change and work through what it would mean for me. They went above and beyond to help me feel comfortable (because as we know, neurodivergent people can struggle with change.) They are ALWAYS there to help when you need assistance with the app and they do so with genuine compassion, care, and kindness.
author: ashleyback

title: Just liars & thieves taking advantage of ADHD impulsivity.
body: This is definitely not an ADHD friendly app!  They lie about features and ease of use to take advantage of ADHD impulsivity. You read their lies and pay for features then find out the truth. I do believe that every person building this app has ADHD & zero communication skills across their teams. Searching for specific instructions is not an option, there is NO search bar. And the “Create a master routine in the routine library” (routine library) doesn’t exist! The whole reason I paid for this app for a year! Features aren’t consistent between iOS devices, much less the web/browser. You can’t add an end date when setting up a repeating task. After adding the task you can go find what needs to be the last one and delete all future. How is that ADHD friendly? The “custom repeat” is not custom!  I use a medication every 3 days but I can’t set that up with one task. NOT ADHD FRIENDLY!!! I could go on but you get the idea.

author: Kate9210

title: The app that helped change my life
body:
I didn’t think that any productivity app could help put me on a path that would lead to my dreams coming true. Yet the techniques and lessons I learned from using Tiimo have helped me to build the skills in such a way that I now do most thing out of habit and need the app less and less. 

That right there is pure magic and should be the point of all apps that are focused on helping people become more organized and especially when they are designed as thoughtfully as Tiimo; with the neurodivergent community in mind. Don’t miss out on the videos and how to tools in the app as they can really teach you things you thought you knew but really could benefit from learning more about. 

I found myself more successful in using Tiimo due to some of the quality of life perks such as the ability to utilize colors and emojis in interface that make it easier for my brain to sort and process the information it is seeing.

It’s essential features like this that help set Tiimo apart from the rest. I also very much appreciate the ability to have multiple profiles. As someone with multiple disabilities and varying needs in my day to day life, I value being able to switch profiles so that I can access different sets of daily tasks.

Not every productivity or organizational app is for everyone, but the flexibility provided by Tiimo means that I’m confident you’ll find something beneficial from giving it a download and trial run. Good luck and enjoy your Adventures in the Apple App Store!

body:

body: I did the free trial and love the concept as someone with ADHD. It seemed perfect. author: Enna-chan

title: Niche. Not for me
body: I feel like this app doesn’t know what it’s supposed to be. As a to do app, there’s so much friction in adding actual tasks. Compared to other to do apps, it takes more taps to add and modify tasks. There’s no natural language parsing. And it lags. As a scheduler, it fails to take into account that rarely does a day go according to plan. You can’t reschedule easily or auto schedule. The focus function is bare bones. As a mood tracker, there are other apps that consolidate and track the metric more insightfully, like being able to draw correlations or directing you to CBT methods. As a calendar, where is two way sync? I think Tiimo tries to do a lot of things, but none of them are executed particularly well. Despite the pretty UI, the functionality isn’t smooth. The web app does show potential—it feels much better to time block on there than in app.

title: Lifetime Purchase, Lifelong Disappointment—Bring Back Routines!
body:
I am one of the loyal users who bought Tiimo outright when the lifetime purchase was an option. I invested in Tiimo specifically for the routines feature, which was a lifeline for my daily structure and productivity. Having ADHD, routines aren’t just a preference—they’re essential. I relied on this app for the flexibility to check off tasks and smoothly switch through routines without a second thought. It was like having a supportive, invisible coach guiding me through my day.

Now, with routines gone, I’m left with a “task with subtasks” workaround that doesn’t switch properly and lacks the seamless flow that routines offered. What am I supposed to do with a ‘lifetime’ app that no longer fulfills its primary function?

Removing such a core feature feels like breaking a promise to those of us who paid for the app as it was. I’d gladly pay a bit extra if that’s what it takes to bring routines back as an add-on, but don’t take away something that was a dealbreaker for so many users. Please reconsider this change, or at least give us a roadmap on whether there’s any hope for a feature revival.

author: Ned cannonmenace

title: The perfect app… until they got rid of routines
body: After years of medical mysteries, I finally got an accurate diagnosis and treatment for an otherwise debilitating sleep disorder. For the first time in my adult life, I realized I could go to college, but I knew I would need help, so I poured myself into researching assistive technologies that could help me manage my day-to-day activities and routines as I adapted to the new experience of college life. I heard so many good things about Tiimo - it kept coming up over and over again in my research, so once I got my new iPad, I purchased the subscription and dedicated myself to learning how to use it. Now, I am a 4.0 student, an orientation leader, and an advocate for my fellow students with disabilities. It's amazing what the right diagnosis, treatment, and assistive technologies can do to level the playing field - I am finally competing with my peers after years of feeling like I could never measure up. I barely graduated high school, but now, I'm the top of my class at my local university. Having a set and scheduled routine is such a big thing for me. A big part of my morning challenges is mental fatigue - I just literally don't have the ability in the mornings to do the mental math and prioritization to quickly figure out on the fly what I need to change if something goes awry. The way the routines feature managed my time and the granularity of the subtasks within each timed activity had been such an absolute game changer for me. I literally cut an hour out of my morning routine once I started using Tiimo because I wasn’t wasting time trying to recalibrate after each activity. This is my biggest executive function deficit and the way this feature just smoothed it right over and allowed me to truly function at full capacity was such a big deal to me. The hours of developing and redeveloping these routines as my needs changed over time were all rendered null and void when the Tiimo team got rid of the routine function (which individually timed each activity in the routine and automatically removed that time from the greater routine) and gave us… One activity with untimed subtasks? Now, instead of being able to see how much time I have left in my routine to know if I’ll be able to catch the bus at a glance, I need to get a calculator out on my phone to see if it would be a waste of time to eat breakfast or not. Additionally, several of my routines were long, with around 20 activities, some of which had subtasks to them, so now, I have to scroll up and down the subtasks list of around 30 items on what used to be a simple routine. The loss of the routines function was hard enough, but the solution you implemented, having subtasks that just lists the item of the routine and the time it takes was also impacted in a recent update that makes checking off those items even harder. I spent ten minutes tonight trying to figure out how to view and check off subtasks from the day menu, only to find that to check off a subtask, you now have to go into the edit menu, check off the subtask, and save it to make sure the items stay checked. Before the update, this was simple and straightforward, but now I have to expend mental energy that I do not have to go through this elongated process, just to check something off of a list. Even worse - the reasoning for the removal of the routines function comes off as incredibly ableist and snarky. I may be one of "only" 300 paying users to utilize the routines function, but I am a paying user and the features that keep me as a Tiimo user are still important! At least give me the option to opt in to a more deluxe membership - I'd gladly pay a few more dollars a month for a feature that has become so critical to my success! I understand that software companies right now are struggling, but is the only option to remove one of the most important features from a paying user? Because what's left isn't enough to maintain my membership.

title: I’m done
body:
I’ve been using this app for ages, and happily paying for it, and Routines is why. It was the one thing that made it ideal for me over other apps (and was so useful to me that it made up for the glitches and other design frustrations). Now Routines have been “simplified” to the point of no longer being useable, as the developers want to make a generic AI list-generator app instead (I already have one, thanks, and it’s one that works better and is much less expensive than this).

Silver lining is I need a new phone anyways, so this is an opportunity to drop some apps like Tiimo that are dead weight and save big on my app subscription costs. I appreciated the convenience of an app that did what Tiimo used to do and I hope some other app is out there that actually cares about the needs of their userbase (see: Tiimo’s predatory subscription model + the fact that they specifically target disabled users for their product. Not a good look!). But worst case, I can replicate Routines with a checklist app and a timer, which seems to fly in the face of their claim that it’s “to hard” to continue to update the feature that sold me on the product in the first place. 

Tiimo, your marketing doesn’t make up for a bad product, even when your target demographic is more vulnerable than most. And lot of us have more time on our hands than you do and we *will* spread the word.
author: Lizzylearnsfrench

title: Do Not Like the Oct 2024 Update
body:
Unless I am missing something, after the update, it does not appear that there is a timer for the individual tasks in a routine. One overall timer for the entire routine is not helpful. I want to know how much time I’m spending on each task, to ensure that I’m on track to finish my routine in the desired amount of time. If I wanted one overall timer, I could just use the built in timer on my phone for free. Additionally, it does not appear that there is a setting that can be changed for the “Anytime” category to appear at the top, instead of “Planned.” And the perpetual “Schedule a Virtual Focus Session” button blocks the view of the task that is displayed behind it when a routine is running.

Previous Review 3 Stars - Inability to Not Import All-Day Events is Disappointing: I frequently use all-day events as reminders (bill due dates, dog’s monthly medication, and future date events that I cannot schedule yet) so on any given day I can have at least 5 - 6 all-day events. Perhaps I’m in the minority, but since I have many other apps that allow me to exclude all-day events, I’m very shocked that this isn’t an option with this app. It discourages me from using the timer because I have several concurrent timers going, and the list of all-day events takes up a decent amount of space in the calendar view. It appears that there is a planned update for this, so I hope that it occurs soon because this feature is really impacting my user experience.

title: ADHD planning hacked
body:
TLDR: syncs with phone calendar instantly, daily review where you can move some tasks/activities to the next day without guilt or any hassle!!

I don’t even remember where I saw this app, maybe an ad on Facebook. I took the plunge. I’ve used it for several days and I’ve been able to get a lot of small projects done in my house. The option to just add anytime activities and get a suggested list of subtasks is awesome. Then you add in an easy way to “reschedule”? And I add something in my Apple calendar and it’s like instant to Tiimo? Better than every other app. One other thing (and I haven’t checked if it’s possible) apps miss is being able to cross over Apple/android. Background: I basically help my sister, she has memory problems, add in my ADHD and everything else I personally need to get done, it can be hard to organize our schedules and make sure she gets reminders, etc. Just a suggestion if it’s not already something existing! :)

title: Very good but important detail overlooked
body: I got excited about this app because the visual scheduling is so easy and enjoyable. I’m all about count downs and this is the only one I’ve been able to find that has a live activity count down which starts automatically. The interface is simple where it needs to be and more complicated in other ways. BUT for all the ease there are two very glaring oversights that make me not willing to extend use past the free trial: 1. If I have a number of events scheduled for “anytime” today and I have blocks of my schedule that are open why aren’t all of those activities suggested when I go to add an activity in the open time slot? Instead I get very limited options: blocks of focus time, or creating an entirely new activity, or. AI suggestions which seem to be utterly random and not helpful. Similarly, I should be able to drag tasks from the “anytime” portion of the calendar into open timeslots. These are such obvious oversights that I am unable to enjoy the app fully.

author: Bill The Man #2

title: An app for ADHD…disgraceful
body:
I tried this for a day and it was not what I was hoping it would be and turned it off. Of course I get a charge for the highest annual subscription two days ago. 

A courtesy email reminder “hey, your trial period is ending in 2 days, please cancel or choose a plan, otherwise you’ll be penalized with the highest annual plan” wouldn’t be that difficult. 

That’s not good business,  ESPECIALLY considering the market you are targeting. I’m quite aware NOW that there is a small place that says you’ll be billed if you don’t cancel so my mistake, but the appearance is that us forgetting is what you’re banking on, taking advantage of the most vulnerable prey. Annual too, that’s just wrong. 

The app may work for some, but it was a hindrance to me. The “do anytime” was a complete waste but the worst part is when something comes up or you’re in a zone and not ready to stop something, it pauses but continues on so the next several tasks just kept on coming, no asking how much more time do you need to rearrange the schedule but it pauses but continues on with the next thing like you can do 5 things at once. It was way more work and caused more chaos than it was worth in my case. 

I’ve turned all notifications off again and will delete the app that you decided I wanted for a whole year.

Unsolicited business advice, but the appearance is shady and in the age of social media, appearances are everything. This could be handled way better and show some kindness to those who are already struggling.

title: Changes are being made for the bottom line NOT consumer
body: I felt so excited to finally have an app that understands the granularity of the ADHD brain and caters to that. Now? It’s all focused on pushing AI and “Tiimo Learn”. I just want an app that delivers on its promises. Now it’s taking away the ONE feature that makes it unique as opposed to Structured or Productive. The Routines feature made this app worth the money. Now it’s just the same while shoving AI down our throats thinking it’s enough to justify charging double the price of those other apps. I just got a yearly subscription just to be told a week later that the app is getting neutered for the sake of “simplicity”. We are not neurotypical! We don’t need that. We need something that understands how we think differently. Now it’s just an app that’s like everyone else. But AI guys! That will make up for it! 🙄

title: Useful but buggy…
body:
I got this app because I needed help visualizing time. I had a bad habit of always running late and wanted to get to work earlier than I was doing before. So far, it’s helped in that regard once I fine tuned my schedule and I consistently used it in the weekdays. While I’m disappointed that manually making checklists is behind a paywall, I still find the premade ones helpful and it’s helped me get through my workdays. But the reason I docked a star is because it’s so buggy in the one area I really need it: the visual timer. 

If I pause the timer on the Home Screen of my phone, there’s a 50% chance it doesn’t actually register and the clock is still running in the app, or I tell it to resume and doesn’t start in the app. This is immensely frustrating, because if I go in the app to check something off and to see how much time I have left, there’s a chance the clock never even started again! Or the timer will say I have one minute left on the home screen but then six minutes in the app. This throws me and my schedule in the app off. How am I supposed to visualize time if the app can’t even keep time too? 😭 I’ll still use the free version but I won’t pay for it until this is fixed.

title: Subscription models are predatory
body:
This app has so much potential but if you’re experimenting with the free version, even the tutorial constantly has you click things that bring up the “NO YOU MUST SUBSCRIBE TO BREAK DOWN A TASK”. 
A subscription model specifically being targeted at neurodivergent people takes advantage of them forgetting small monthly charges and bumps prices later. Its designed to have an gratifying flow to set it up, and then will break flow repeatedly in ways that will annoy vulnerable people into a quick sub. Then it does the bait and switch of “try for $3/mo or save with $36 a year in advance.” This is an advertising tactic that works really well on impulsive people, particularly those suffering from a mental health crisis. 
I would happily pay $10 one time for this app after a testing period of a few days. But I’m not giving money to intentionally exploitative subscription models.

title: Still has issues.
body:
I like this app, it provides a lot more flexibility and features than most planner apps. Great options for taggings, colors, and icons. Great for recurring tasks, unscheduled tasks that take a certain amount of time, calendar import, etc. And the timer features are the best. But in other ways, the app is too unreliable and distracting. 
UI has issues on an older iphone SE with a smaller screen. Some menus are slightly cut off at the bottom of the screen. I also wish that most menus let you see more tasks on screen, I feel like this app often takes too much scrolling. 
Too many popup ads for random events and features I don’t care about, even though I pay for a subscription. I need a planner app. Your blogposts and classes are extra distractions that I don’t need, and the app gives no option to disable those popups. 
Widgets, notifications, and watch app are convenient but unreliable, especially if you don’t open the app frequently. It’s still nice to have, but it makes it just a bit harder to justify the subscription fee.

title: Beware of these people.
body:
I tried to step out for one day. Just one day. I clicked the free trial button and very next day I decided the app was not for me and I went to cancel the trial only to find they charged me for an entire entire year subscription.  I reached out to them about this they refused to return my money. They claimed that I had also tried to free trial this app in 2020. Hello! I have ADHD! I don’t remember that. And even if it did happen, it makes no sense to me that my punishment for accidentally re-downloading the same app twice in 5 years is a $45 charge. Are you useless than 24 hours of this service. 

I warn you against doing any business with people who have such shady practices. As for the app itself, I feel like I was a victim of hype from various ADHD influencers. It’s just another task management app. Nothing life-changing.

 I prefer to use Structured. It makes more sense. And it’s much much cheaper at only $15 a year. It has a web app. Tasks that take different amount of times are  diffeeent sizes and you can set an energy budget so you know how much tasks take lot of you. 

As for Tiimo, I don’t think the way that you add task is very intuitive. There is also no way to add a multi step routine each day. The AI task breakdown is nice, but structured also has that feature. For for nearly $45 a year— feel cheated. Please return my money Tiimo. What you’re doing is not fair or right.
author: Nia Dx

title: Wanted to like it
body:
I’m a psychologist with ADHD and have tried a lot of different apps to keep me on track.
First of all, pretty useless if you don’t pay for it. And not worth the money bc it’s stressful.
 
Personally, the app itself was super overwhelming and made me even more stressed. I didn’t even know where to start. In fact, I couldn’t even start and am deleting the app and canceling my subscription. Too complicated for an app that’s supposed to be for people with ADHD. 

You are better off using the free reminders app on your iphone and the timer on your clock app. In fact, you’re better off using notes on your iphone and making a checklist. Don’t even give this app a try.

author: Cocoa pup

title: Realizing how truly valuable the app is!
body: Diagnosed late in life. So many things ingrained in my thinking that I now know are caused by my neurodivergent brain. Between seeking help from a neuropsychologist and therapist and finding Tiimo, I am beginning to feel like there is light at the end of the tunnel! I found Tiimo by accident and am staying for the amazing support from staff, and the classes, and the Body Doubling sessions, and the calendar and the gentle nudges from the app that are helping me see things in a totally different way. author: Puakia

title: Just need this one thing…
body:
The design of the app is very aesthetically appealing and easy to use. I really, really, really want to use this app on a regular basis. However, the way tasks auto start is an issue for me. If I start one task ten minutes late then my whole Tiimo schedule is messed up unless I manually pause tasks as I go. I think an easy way to fix this would be where you have the option to manually press “completed task” when you’re done and *then* it automatically moves to the next task after this. If you haven’t finished the task yet but you’re over the time limit you set for it, your next tasks just sit there waiting and don’t start until you’re done with this one. This way there’s no breaks in the routine but your whole schedule isn’t messed up if you’re a few minutes late.

Please Tiimo, let me know if you plan on doing something about this soon. Like I said I really want to use Tiimo but for the meantime I think I will have to use a different app.
author: Super Awesome woohoo

author: rvhtujv

title: Paying to be reminded on a reminding app!?
body:
Do not get me wrong. Tiimo WAS a fantastic apps before this update; it was free to create a checklist and have widgets on your iOS device, but now it is basically useless.

 I stopped using Tiimo briefly after starting school because everyone has their own schedule, but I started using it again this summer because I have all the time in the world and need to keep track of it because of my neurodivergence and OH BOY. The first thing I saw was a subscription ad, which is fine since the app is still fictional without the extra abilities, right? WRONG. Apparently, if you want to create a checklist to meet your particular needs or if you want to be reminded before you activity, you must pay. 

I could understand if the membership was for other bonuses, such as virtual learning sessions or expert courses, but what about the app's overall purpose? What's the sense of having the app if it serves no function for individuals who don't have the money or who may not be able to subscribe at all? It's very aggravating; yes, the app is still usable, but it's not practical.

title: Too Difficult To Use, Too Many Steps
body:
I really wanted to love this app :( I wanted it to be easy to set my days and create a better way of following it. There's something off about the flow this app creates. 

I would highly suggest an import function for the Reminders app that Apple has. This is the best thing about the "Structured" app. I can easily just ask Siri to add a reminder to my day while I'm driving or shopping into a specific list which will then automatically sync into the inbox on structured for me to drag and drop into a space my day or week has. 
I couldn't find an easy way to add my reminders unless I had both apps open which was just too much back and forth.
author: Krissspaaaaa

title: Needs more useful choices, less blogging
body:
Generally, I love having the app, but I’m beginning to think of exploring other options. 

***With every update, my to-do list (now called inbox??) that I took a lot of time to enter, disappears!!!

I agree with another review about your schedule just running without you whether you do it or not.  If you sleep in or something prevents you from starting the ideal schedule you pre-entered, it just starts greying out things you haven’t done and says you’re in the middle of something you haven’t started yet.  I’d rather it force ME to say - ok, begin my day now, and then proceed with the entered length of times I entered.  Or make ME tap - yes, begin this as scheduled in 5 minutes, and make ME tap that it’s done rather than just greying it out when the time is up.  If I don’t click done, it shouldn’t move on.  This should be obvious to people catering to ADHD.  The only way to kinda do this is to start and then pause, which isn’t effective.  I’m aware of rescheduling, but this isn’t really what I want to do.  

And as someone who has premium, what’s the difference between that and premium plan??  I don’t want the seminars and blogs that are now part of premium learn, that’s for sure - but it’s in my face all the time.  Stop with the fanciness and make the basic planning / schedule app that we all needed better with more setting choices and increased functionality.  Please.

author: Tzalez

title: Negative stars
body:
Don’t bother with this app, the 7 day trial is a trap!! I forgot to cancel and I asked for a refund 1 day after it was charged to my card and it wasn’t eligible for refund. I appealed the decision and after the review, they still didn’t refund me. I’m out $37 because I didn’t cancel before the trial.

They want to help people with ADHD get organized but they surely aren’t kind to them. The first thing they should teach the user is how to set a reminder to cancel before the trial period BUT setting reminders are MESSY! It preloads a “start” and “end” your day prompt that clutters the task screen. 
Pro tip: people with ADHD need as little clutter as necessary or else they will fidget with how to remove it or get distracted.

Why is the schedule messy with things we don’t need. I don’t care that I wasted money on this stupid app, I literally downloaded a free temp and did one myself. Those of you who like it for the AI assist, just plug in your task to chat gpt and ask to simplify your task or “can you put this task in bullet points?” And it will do it for you. Copy and paste onto a calendar where, when you click the day, a side note pad will show and paste that on there! You’ll more than likely remember it’s there and more likely to do it! The thing that got me was trying to reschedule tasks that I didn’t do and when I inserted the date, it wouldn’t show up on the new date. In fear I would lose that task, I just started using a post it note. 

This app is so disorganized and not helpful for people with adhd. You don’t need this app. Trust me. Don’t waste your money. 

It is a completely reasonable request to ask for a refund for a product I used for less that 10 days (and for 6, was never even opened!) and for a calendar with crappy UI. Even most stores give 30 days.

title: A Lifesaver for the Neurodivergent Community
body:
Last update: add a “focus mode” that reduces clutter and I’ll be the happiest person in the world. 

Edit: I still love this app, but it’s too cluttered for me now. I understand the intent of the “Learn” tab, but it’s more stuff on the Home Screen of the app that I’ll never touch. The lofi beats are great but you hear the same track after about an hour, and that isn’t great for my focus. As someone with ADHD, the app simply has too much crammed into a space that’s suppose to help me think, not overwhelm me.

As a neurodivergent individual, Tiimo has been an absolute lifesaver for me. Having used it daily for over two years, I can confidently say it's an essential part of my routine. The app provides the structure and checklists I need to navigate my day effectively. Its AI feature is a standout, allowing me to get started quickly and’s easily on any activity. I recently used it to help me create a list to manage panic attacks. Tiimo's intuitive design and tailored approach make it unrivaled in the market. It's not just an app for me; it's a daily companion that brings order and peace to my life. I'm a loyal user for life and highly recommend it to anyone seeking a reliable, supportive organizational tool.

title: This is far and away the worst planner I have used
body: And I've tried a few task management tools along the way, such as Sunsama, Routine, Amplenote, and TickTick, among others. However, Tiimo stands out as a particularly challenging tool to use. It lacks integration capabilities with other popular apps like TickTick and ClickUp, which means manually entering tasks into Tiimo's cumbersome interface. Moreover, making changes to tasks and deleting them is unnecessarily complicated and unintuitive. After accidentally overstaying my free trial, I was determined to make Tiimo work for me. title: A waste
body:

1. The app asks to track your activity if you have iOS 17, and if you decline it will pop up and ask every time you open the app. This is so distracting if you have ADHD, for one, and two: I didn’t pay your insane price for a subscription just to get continually asked to do your marketing research for you. Fix this! It’s ugly and insulting.

2. Every time I try to add or modify a routine, there’s a 75% chance the app will crash or delete the routine.

3. No way to see if your anytime tasks will fit in your day.

4. Notifications work sporadically. I need them to give me haptic notifications on my watch and that goes through maybe 30% of the time.

5. Extremely cluttered onboarding and a ton of fancy corporate Memphis graphics but little education on how to use the app functionally. Maybe that’s because it barely functions.

Anyway, wish I hadn’t spent $30 on this so I hope I save anyone reading this some money.

author: Norywinslow

title: After Years, More Stressful Than Helpful
body:
I’ve been trying to use this app for years and stick around for the changes, but the problems have yet to be resolved. I’ve submitted these over time. I have stopped using the app for a while, hoped it’s gotten better, and returned multiple times. The restrictions on the free version have gotten terrible during that time; if I want to try the app again and see if it’s worth my time and money (that I really don’t have to begin with), I have to get the paid version to even edit older activities I’ve already set the last time I used it, even just to change the day. My complaints are the same as others and it has, overall, caused me more anxiety, stress, and grief. No refund could cover the amount of work I’ve put into using this app only for it to not function correctly. 

Examples of some problems: new activities will disappear. Ones you’ve deleted will reappear. Re-organized lists will rearrange themselves to where you’d just moved them from. The timer on your phones Lock Screen does not sync with the timer in the app if you pause or add time to it. Right now, I have given up because an activity I paused days ago is showing that it needs to be finished, despite that same activity having refreshed and started for today. I tried to update and restart, and now I have an empty activity running that won’t go away. Again, these issues haven’t been addressed and have been a problem for a very long time. 

I’m disheartened because I really want to support this app and their team; I’ve been suggesting it to others with the promises that things should be fixed up soon. I truly do not see how this app is “autistic/ADHD friendly” because all it did was take a calm organization time I had set aside for myself and made it an anxious mess that never gets cleaned up because the app can’t save itself correctly. I’m sad because I sincerely need an app like this, but I am now distrustful of the targeted neurodivergent and queer ads.

author: Jensen Hills

title: End up frustrated every time
body:
I really love Tiimo, I do, but the app never really seems to actually get easier to use with updates. 

There is still an issue with calendar syncing.  If you accidentally delete a calendar synced event from your timeline, you’re out of luck on ever getting it back on Tiimo.  I’ve tried un-syncing and re-syncing my calendar, signing out and back in, it never restores the event in Tiimo even though the event is still visible in my calendar.  It’s extremely frustrating to not have a fix for this, it almost eliminates the benefits of being able to sync calendars in the first place if you have to spend the extra time manually inputting things that should show up with that calendar.  Syncing across devices also still needs work..they never reflect changes made within the other. (Ex: Accidentally deleted a calendar synced event on my iPad, but it still shows up on my phone. Any edits I make will not sync across devices. So weird.)

Also, I really wish they would give us an update that has an option to have routines and events read out-loud to you.  This would be particularly helpful for your users with dyslexia, vision disabilities, etc.
author: Bl0ndeZ0mbie

title: Absolutely not for neurodivergents
body: The app is aesthetically pleasing, I’ll give it that. Aside from looking pretty, it’s nearly functionless. Way over priced and doesn’t function as advertised. As a neurodivergent, I feel like this app is not designed with my best interest in mind and the developers are just profiting from a group of people who truly need an app like this. I’ve reported issues multiple times and nothing has been fixed. 1. You can’t organize tasks. That’s right. You try to move them around and they go right back to where they started. 2. Once finished, a task stays where it is so you have to scroll through a list of completed/incomplete tasks, and like I said you can’t reorganize them. Or you can try and cross your fingers 3. Recurring tasks are limited since you can only schedule them in weekly or monthly increments. You can’t do a 10 day or 6 month recurring task. Which honestly are the hardest tasks to remember. 4. You can’t reschedule your recurring tasks. You have to send the task to another day (and if it shows up, sometimes it doesn’t) then you have to re-create the recurring task for the new day and completely delete the task and all recurring tasks from the day it was originally due. 5. Support insists you send them screenshots and videos or else they ignore the issue. 6. No task integration from other apps. A great idea for an app but executed poorly. I waste so much time trying to organize the tasks and to get it to work it defeats the purpose. I wouldn’t pay for it again and I would urge others to look elsewhere before trying to organize your life with this app. I spent so much time setting everything up it feels like such a waste. It’s just a prettier less functional version of apple tasks.

title: Good, but a beta at best
body:
Let me just say I really like the app. The creators have a page where users are able to submit features they would like to see and vote for others they’d like to see. I love this open conversation with the users. 

The app has a lot of features I really enjoy. The visual times are nice, the routines are nice. I paid for the full version to use the checklists. If you just need the visual timers and a loose plan for your day, this will work well for you. 

For me, I have severe ADHD and need to plan out even the tiniest details and be ready for last minute changes. Tiimo isn’t too great at that. Once you’ve started an activity the only way to end it is to complete it. You can let it end, and then reschedule but it’s clunky. Multiple times the timer wheel has been stuck no matter how many times I try to complete the event. 

Overall I think this project will be really great—in time. The app has lots of bugs, and a lot of features don’t work how you think they would be able to. It seems like the creators are very responsive and helpful, so I’m hoping this app will improve with time.

title: Good app
body:

Premium allows for more customization options (colors, app icon, tag changes), so if that’s important for you then the premium version would be suited for you

For the developers’ consideration:
•Implement a way for the user to create multiple tasks at once (similar to how you can create tasks for routines, but for standalone tasks as well) 
•In the “my day” tab, the buttons to add an activity and for the library should be on the left side since the right side has a purpose (to edit or delete you have to open a menu on the right side)
•Implement a way to hide or collapse tasks and routines that have been completed that day (similar to how you can collapse the “planned” and “to do anytime” sections)

title: Has changed my day to day
body:
I am a paper planner girl, but this app has helped integrate technology in a way that helps me to focus. It also helps me to purposefully plan time blocks for decompressing. 

This app is so visually appealing, while also giving you some creativity in how your to do or appointment blocks appear. 

I love that my phone app calendar events are built into each day also. Another feature that is amazing is the Brain Dump log. Here you can add several thoughts, ideas, and to dos and then push them out into your schedule if it is something you want to get done. Or it stays in the Brain Dump section until you have time to look it over. There’s also the ability to reschedule something you didn’t get done. The app has built in routines (like winding down before bed) and you can also create your own. 

I highly recommend it to anyone who isn’t usually a planner because this is so different and might actually work for you.
author: Zully Hernandez

title: Great idea, poor performance
body:
I was so excited about this app when I first got it that I jumped into the premium subscription almost right away. Been using it for a little over a month and it feels like the more I use it the more I use it the worse it gets. It has so many bugs. As soon as one thing gets fixed another problem pops up. I know it can take some time to work the kinks out, but  as I understand this app has been around for a few years now, it shouldn’t feel this rough. The biggest problem I’m dealing with currently is being unable to put activities in the correct day. They always default to today! I have to mess around with it to get it to go where I intended. It’s incredibly frustrating and counter productive. Also, the lock screen timer only seems to work half the time, and there’s no rhyme or reason to it. 
Aside from the bugs, there’s other things that could make this app better. I wish it was more customizable. It would be great if the app didn’t automatically mark tasks as done just because the timer is up, and instead asked if I did the task and sent reminders until I completed it. Otherwise it’s too easy to forget to do things or leave them unfinished. I also wish I could drag the anytime items and place them in between scheduled activities so that they sit in the general portion of the day that I intend to do them. This is supposed to be a visual planner, but the way it currently stands, my tasks are all out of order. 
Anyway, I appreciate what the developers are trying to do here and I’m sure it’s not an easy task, but I just expected more, especially since I’m paying to use it and it doesn’t seem like they offer refunds.

author: STJTx2

title: Has the potential to be a dream come true app
body:
As someone who seeks out customization options in every thing I own, especially apps, this app won me over. I get to upload my own icons!! Pro 1: built in timers (a rare but important habit tracking feature),   

Pro 2: customization ability 

Pro 3: tasks can be reset 

 Pro 4: widgets are well built and aesthetic.

 Con 1: timer minutes don’t keep the minutes I set them for! Such an odd bug. Support team quickly replied however and development team is on the case. But that bug is a huge problem for my personal use case. If I have a 2 minute timer, I need it to be 2 minutes. Not 1 not 4 not 12.

Con 2: apparently I never set one of my tasks as a daily. This is surprisingly easy to not set up in this app. One of the less intuitive aspects imo. As a result I missed a daily commitment and now I have to start my commitment over (it’s part of a course I’m in, and is required to do a certain amount of actions daily. Can’t miss any or I fail.) this kind of issue costs me! 

 Con 3: the videos built into this app. They NEVER go away?! AND they have a weird agenda about them too (injecting testerone???!!) please at least let us hide videos in our app, or close them out for good. Not all lifestyles are the same. And many of us with autism need a quiet app environment. Not loud visuals. 

 Overall: for many of us we pour our important tasks into apps like this. Broken features are devastating. Yet due to the potential of this app, I hope it gets some fixes.

author: Stang0767

title: Feel a bit taken advantage of, but my bad
body:
Timmo simply didn’t work for me. I have tried a couple other apps like this with the time blocking, and my main frustration is the assumption that I’m actually going to do the tasks when I have them listed.

It also simply felt clunky and needed a lot of maintenance to use throughout the day.

I am a physically disabled, neurodivergent stay at home mom. I do have several things that happen daily without fail, such as my kids’ bedtime routines, going to appointments, etc. However, as a stay at home mom, (I have 6 kids, 5 of whom are also neurodivergent) it’s up to me how my days flow. Given what kind of “mood” my ADHD is in it could be a productive, hyper-focused day, or basically the exact opposite.

The limited version of the app is available for free, however the real functionality and features are behind the paywall.

I wish I could remember exactly what it was that I was working on adding as I was attempting to set the app up after initially down loading it, but the free version had a limit of “X” number of something.

I needed more than “X” and very impulsively decided to purchase the app. I paid for the yearly subscription to save money.

It was only a matter of days until I figured out the app was not compatible with me (and I definitely think it was a compatibility issue versus Timo not being effective). Time management and productivity is very personal.

I just looked up my subscription and it expires October 19, 2023.

I did chalk this experience up to another impulsive ADHD decision that was a waste of my valuable money. However, I did decide to leave this review on April 1 (Autism acceptance month) when I saw Timmo advertising as being “Autism friendly“.

It was the “ADHD Friendly” claim that caught my eye in October 2022, (which is ADHD awareness month).

As a Neurodivergent individual, Advocate and mother of Neurodivergent kids, this personally really stung.

Neurodivergent individuals are likely more familiar than they wish with some of the common traits, including impulsivity. It’s definitely a big one for me one that has cost a significant amount of money over the years.

My boys and I are all on Social Security, and as I have said, it was my choice to pay for the app. Even if I had changed my mind the same day of the purchase (I know I stopped using I t within a few days, and tried a couple more times with no luck) it would’ve been impossible to get a refund with the subscription that I chose, and I chose the annual subscription with the intention of saving money. As we all know, paying for something we don’t use is a waste I wish Timmo would offer a free trial period of a minimum of 7 days. (I was recently given a 14-day-trial of a different app, and based on how helpful that app has been for me, I decided to purchase a six month subscription, and my decision was partly influenced by the 14-day free trial. I would not have been able to truly understand the features and benefits of the app, without access to everything that paid members receive. I’m very glad to see that this app seems to help quite a few people (based on the reviews) and you can call me sensitive, but I feel pretty creeped out by seeing an advertisement for being “autism friendly” that appeared just after midnight on the very first day of autism acceptance month. It seems very predatory to me, and the reason I am leaving this review.

title: Helps my ADHD, but lacks necessary features
body:
I have to say, I really enjoyed this app. I love the user interface and the ability to create custom tasks and groupings. However, navigation within the app is awkward and clunky. It is time-consuming and awkward to schedule and reschedule tasks— every time you need to edit some thing, it requires going into each task individually, and if this timing intrudes onto a subsequent event, then you need to edit that subsequent events time manually and so on, and so forth. 

This app would benefit from two big features,
1. The ability to drag and drop items within the days schedule. This would be a fast and visual way to organize the day.
2. A desktop interface for this app, either available through the macOS web store, or as a Web app.

title: Great for sleep blindness! Not easy to adjust.
body:
* I love how the big circle shows me the passage of time as I go through my work day routines. - I have disabled my iPhone’s auto-lock so that I can keep this on my desk near my keyboard!

* I love the audible cues telling me it’s almost time to start the next task or a routine is finishing… - I’ve turned up the volume so I don’t miss that.  

* I love that I can “import” my calendar to show my appointments in line with my routines (to check for conflicts) and then un-import them so I can keep using the alerts from iPhone calendar for my appointments so I don’t confuse the audio alerts. 

But…

There are some improvements I’d like to see.  I have noticed that the help desk is responsive and it seems the developers are working hard. So…

1. I would really like the ability to turn off alerts for certain tasks.  Right now it’s all or nothing.  I would like to customize my work day routine to alert on the start of some activities, and 5 minutes before other activities, and then halfway through my longest activities.  

2. I *need* to be able to customize each type of alert.  I need to be able to recognize that a particular sound means “your activity is starting in 5 minutes” or “your activity is half over”.   Those sounds must be immediately recognizable to me or they aren’t useful; they are just noise and merely distractions.

title: So Close, Save for Bugs and Crashes
body: Tiimo is a fantastic idea of an app for those with ADHD and other neurodiverse people! But it is so incredibly buggy even with the update and it’s left me frustrated when trying to habit stack my days and structure my routines. Every time I remove a routine or calendar event, I have to restart the app to see the results or the app crashes in the process of moving events around. It’s really difficult to restart timed routines, and it can feel really defeating when you start a routine late (such as a morning routine because you needed some extra z’s) and it starts to feed to the shame cycle that all many neurodiverse people struggle with, especially time management or being behind. Even editing routine templates before inserting them into my schedule became tedious work because every little edit would take multiple tries to save it, especially checklists or descriptions under each task. It was easy to become frustrated with the app because you can see the bones of what will be a great UI interface and experience. I was really hopeful that Tiimo would be my go-to planning and task management app, but it just doesn’t clear the bar in its current iteration. It is clear how passionate the dev team is for the community it is trying to support. I am grateful for this company, and I hope they keep working on it!

author: gorogoroluv

title: Disappointed
body:
I heard about Tiimo and how it was specifically designed and developed to help neurodivergent people better organize and manage their time, days, and schedules. Being an adult who has struggled with ADD my entire life, I’m sure you can imagine how it peaked my interest.

Before downloading the app, I only had a vague understanding of the overall concept of how it worked but I figured, like with most apps, there would a tutorial on how to use it. So, hopeful and optimistic I downloaded the app to use on my iPhone and signed up for a year subscription with a 7 day free trial that carried the option to canceled anytime within the 7 day free trial without being charged.

Today is day 6 of my trial and sadly I don’t feel like I know much more about how to use the app than I did the day I downloaded it. There wasn’t any kind of tutorial on how to set-up or begin using the app. The first time I opened the app after downloading it asked me to log in then asked me to turn on notifications. Since I figured I would be about to turn notifications on later I opted not to turn any notifications on until I had a chance to check it out and set it up. After clearing the notification prompt it took me the “Right now” page, which was obviously blank because nothing had been created or scheduled yet, but that was it, there was nothing to direct me on where to go or what to do next. I was just left to figure out this app on my own which, for someone with ADD, isn’t exactly easy and the app isn’t particularly user friendly either.

However, because I had heard so many good things about this app I still wanted try it out. So I click on “Me” at the bottom of the screen which took me to what appeared to be settings and some information with links to blogs on different Neurodivergent subjects and management strategies, none of which were helpful in setting up this app.

Next I clicked on the Help Center link which took me to a website with Tech Support options for the Android, Apple IOS, Browser Versions of the app, and  one option for General support and inquiries. The General support link took me to a page that seemed like it might have some answers. There were four categories on the General page: What is Tiimo?, Technical, Subscription & Billing, and Contact Us. Under “What is Tiimo?” the first link was “How do I get started!”, finally, answers…or so I thought.

The information provided on “How do I get started!” was less of a step-by-step guide to setting-up and using the app and more of, or rather, actually a list of their “top 5 tips”. Which of the these 5 tips only 1 maybe 2 of them had anything to do with set things up in the app. The 5 tips listed in order are:

1) Set your schedule - Which is 4 sentences about how it takes time to fully integrate Tiimo and recommendations when to plan out your weekly schedule.

2) Create an activity, Create smaller steps with checklists, and Create a routine - Which instructs you on how to create an activity but they only provide screenshots on how to create a check list and a routine without actually explaining how to do it. 

3) Block out Free time - All they tell you here is not to over schedule yourself to make sure your day has planned breaks and blocs of free time but they don’t tell you A) if this is something you “Create” like the activities and routines or B) if it is, then how to create it.

4) Have fun! - They talk about how you can personalize Tiimo with icons, colors, and uploaded photos but again nothing how to do so.

5) Look back on the past week - Which is about discussing when Tiimo was helpful and and when it wasn’t over the previous week. Then using that information to continue setting up and fine tuning the app.

Not helpful.

So I went back to the General page and found a link for “Using Tiimo” I clicked it and it took me to another page that just says “Check out this really cool guide for you here!” The word “here!” is in bold to indicate another link. When I click on “here!” and it took me to yet another website claiming to help you get started with the app but the links that were listed started out with 1) Decide which devices to use, 2) Download the app, suscribe and sign up, 3) Get started which just took me right back to the 5 tips I previously mentioned.

At this point I had been battling my ADD for 6 days struggling to keep myself interested and focused long enough to figure out this darn app but after 6 days of feeling like I’d been running in circles, I was done. I don’t think I have ever had this much trouble, or any trouble for that matter, figuring out and using an app or a program, but for 6 days I tinkered, muddled, played, and messed with this app. I searched for any helpful information online and on social media all just to figure out and actually use this app.

No app should be this difficult nor take this much time to figure out, especially not one that is supposed to be designed and marketed specifically to help neurodivergent people; but if it’s not possible to make it less difficult to figure out and use, then you should at least have a Neurodivergent-friendly tutorial on how to set-up, integrate, and use the app. Although, several shorter tutorials might be better than one long tutorial for users who may struggle with focusing, holding interest, or remembering a lot of new information thrown at them all at once. These tutorials should be easily accessible, available to repeat anytime, and personally I prefer interactive tutorials. Physically going through a the actions of a new process helps me understand and remember it vs. listening to or reading about it.

I am truly glad this app has helped so many people. I was really hopeful that it could help me too but unfortunately it just left me frustrated, exhausted, and disappointed.

author: simsdvmphph

title: Very Happy ADHD Apple Watch User!
body:
I am really impressed with this app! I was expecting it to be a disappointment, as frankly most apps are, but this one has been a delightful surprise. I LOVE that not only does it have powerful capabilities on the Apple Watch (as opposed to claiming it works on the AW, but only providing one basic function as is typical for third party AW apps), but that it has a COMPLICATION for the AW! I am so appreciative of this!!! It boggles my mind how many developers put out AW compatible apps without bothering to go the extra step and create the corresponding complication! So thank you for that!!! 

I do have a few suggestions (I know, like everyone else). First, ADD folks tend to be very visual and color coding is often a big part of a useful organization system. The icons and color options for the dots are great, but I would like the ability to color code the whole routine or activity box as well. Also, having routines or activities that run simultaneously/overlap show up side-by-side on the screen. Finally, the ability to drag/drop unscheduled routines or activities to spots between scheduled things on any given day.

body:
Could be a great app but it’s missing some obvious conveniences, making the app incredibly tedious to set up. Setting up a routine on iOS is maddening. If you edit a routine after you’ve already added it to your plan, the edited parts don’t carry over to your plan. So you have to go back to your plan to delete the unedited version of the routine. What’s worse, when you edit a routine, the time and day and repeating get deleted. So you have to recreated them. Also, on iOS, rearranging the order of the tasks in a routine is a real pain. 

Another terrible thing about the app, there is nothing to track tasks that are not completed on the day assigned. You could easily forget to reassign them. Also, to be truly helpful, this app would have a persistent reminders.

author: thepuma77

title: Without the bugs, this is 100% a 5 star app!
body:
I never write app reviews, but this app has made my ADHD so much more manageable! The visual aspects and using routines have been so helpful. I also love that I can use the notes section to make a running to do list that can quickly be popped into my daily schedule. 

Tiimo does better than what the iOS calendar, reminders, and notes apps did for me all together. I will definitely keep using it but a few of the bugs that have been really annoying are:

1. It’s nearly impossible to check off checklists on my Apple Watch, it just glitches out and won’t check off. It would be AWESOME to just use my watch for my “right now” tasks during the day, but I won’t even bother with it now.

2. When my “right now” task finishes, it doesn’t always go to the next task in my routine without me backing out of that tab and then going back to it.

3. Checking off a checklist and not ending the activity will often uncheck all the bullet points.

4. The worst one; widgets often won’t work. A sort of blank template placeholder will show up instead.

Despite the bugs, I seriously appreciate this app. I really hope they get fixed soon though because they’re really frustrating at times.

title: Time blindness
body: I love this app.It has helped me so much with routines and it also helps my kids. we are all neurodivergent here so this is been a great help for our house. One feature I would love to see added would be a Calendar hourly view like a block schedule. I have time blindness,I’ve noticed when scheduling on this app that I will cram too many things together, double book, or the opposite I’ll leave giant chunks of time open, that I did not notice was open, when I actually need to be doing something. Also being able to see my whole week at a glance in the app, like on the web browser, would be helpful. especially since the routines that you create in the app don’t show up on the web browser.

body:
This app has been a lifesaver for my ADHD. It checks all the boxes- easy to schedule tasks, syncs with Apple Watch for easy tracking of next tasks, seamlessly keeps me moving throughout my day, ready-made routines, can be accessed via desktop anywhere (!!!!!!), and most importantly: easy to REORDER things and they magically get rescheduled correctly (omg this is probably the main reason I come back to Tiimo vs others). They keep updating the app and I just re-subscribed after finding out my old sub ended and other apps just didn’t do it for me. They either took too long to add a task (a deadly thing for ADHD brain) or restructuring the day was just AWFUL. Back to Tiimo it was.
One suggestion I have for making the latter even more seamless would be to have time slots visible during the  blank day to make scheduling tasks even easier (instead of having to select a time when creating or editing a task, just dragging it into the correct time slot or clicking/dragging he time slot to create a task would make it even easier for people like us with executive dysfunction.
Please, please do not stop supporting this app. <3

title: Would absolutely love but one GLARING error
body:
So this app is (almost) everything I’ve been looking for, so I truly hope this bug is updated soon, because to me this app could be as invaluable to me as Notion (and I live by Notion).

Time zones…pesky pesky time zones.
It doesn’t seem to recognize your phone’s time zone, or allow for users across multiple time zones.

For example, I have a work phone set in PST, but I live in CST so my personal phone is set in CST. With google calendar, if I set an event on my CST phone, it will make the correct conversion to PST when the google cal app is opened on my work phone. 

However, if trying to set up tasks in Tiimo on my CST phone, when I open the app on my PST phone, the task still shows in CST. That means I can mark “start” on a task in my work phone and accidentally skip hours of tasks on my CST phone. 

Just wish it was more multi-time zone friendly but alas, maybe I need to stick with google calendar
