author: itsapalindrome

title: Unique and worth it
body:
I’m an oddball and have tried every type of todo and productivity system under the Sun. I recently checked out Tiimo and have been loving it so far. 

The focus on structure, repetition, and focused time is so critical to how a lot of us work best - if you’re trying to do a James Clear Atomic Habits practice, there are few apps around the App Store this dedicated to that vision. 

Another huge difference for me is the dedication to breaking through the design ceilings in productivity app land - at the end of the day, 80% of every single todo app looks like a checklist with maybe a calendar and notes - they all look and feel the same after a while! Tiimo imagines a different way to work and visualizes it in a beautiful and innovative way. 

Same with the support and roadmap for Apple Watch - again for a neurodivergent like me, Apple Watch robust features are non negotiable for me - too many distractions on phone and tablet! 

Now the “bad news” is that this product is in BETA. There are bugs, syncing is a tad more bumpy than a fully established app would be, and there are some odd UI kinks and tiny feature gaps that might frustrate some users who come here from something like a Todoist. 

But it’s fully worth using for me today - maybe with hanging on to a couple apps for other parts of my workflow until Tiimo’s next few releases are under the belt. 

5/5 for the execution so far, the community feedback on their roadmap board, and most of all for their vision! It’s clear they truly “get” the challenges a lot of us face that traditional todo apps don’t help with. 

This is one to support and hope they grow and crush it!
author: Podcast EnjoyerR

title: Problems & Suggestions
body: Here’s some problems I came across. (1) I have vision problems and the times in My Day are a strain to see. I suggest enlarging the font. (2) The widget will say “Right now” for a task that isn’t happening now or soon. It’ll say that for a task an hour away. To avoid confusion, I suggest it say”Upcoming” for tasks that aren’t due yet and “Right now” when it is due. (3) When I complete a task early, I’ll still get a reminder to do that task and it’ll still appear on the widget. It doesn’t matter if I complete the circle and get confetti or if I go to My Day and delete it. It still shows. (4) I don’t always get reminded to do tasks even though I selected that option. A few times, I’ve checked my phone only to see a task halfway done. Very frustrating. (5) I love that I get to choose my own icons, but I suggest the window they first appear in be a circle rather than rectangle., so I can size it correctly. A few times, the final circle has cut off my image and I’ve had to resize it and the app saves both images. Being able to delete an image you no longer want would be helpful, too. (6) Sometimes I’ll add an item to a checklist I want to delete but there seems to be no way to delete it. The only option is to overwrite it but there’s nothing to overwrite. I want to delete. I’d also like to be able to slip in a task in the middle without having to overwrite the entire list. I’m deleting this app for now because the reminders are too unreliable, but if that gets fixed, I’ll come back. I’m a visual learner and I like the visual aspect of this.
author: Gm1234gm

title: Yes! Life/ADHD Friendly!
body:
This app is great!  I was recently diagnosed with ADHD as an adult and I’ve been trying to find tools that fit me…instead of putting stone of energy into doing things a neurotypical way and then either not succeeding or being excessively tired.

I’m not great at building habits or following through.  But this app is helpful in a lot of ways…

1) It helps me break things down.  It can be super overwhelming to get started…or easy to forget something that makes a task that much harder to do.  As I’m starting a task, I can look at the breakdown to get setup/mentally prepped.  And if I forget what I’m doing partway through - I can check again!!

2) It makes me think about time. Im always late, overcommitting, or unable to get to things because I run out of time.  As I’m setting things up in the app (which is actually a fun task for me) I am forced to think about time.  And when I see my day laid out with what I want to do, I’m often surprised about how much time I’ll need to actually accomplish things.  Seeing it like that helps keep me motivated to stay on track - or I’ll run out of time!

3) Yes to the colors and icons!!!  Im suuuuper visual - and I definitely get a dopamine hit from things that are color coded.  I keep a single color for a task so it is easier to identify what is grouped together.  And I just have fun picking icons for tasks or adding pics of my dog for all of pup care tasks - and of course it makes me happy to look at his face in the app haha.

Has this app fixed the challenges I have because if ADHD- absolutely not, and nothing will!  That’s not a reasonable expectation for any app.  But it helps me keep more energy for myself and keep in a more peaceful mindset - instead of needing to use it to remember things over and over again, feeling as stressed when planning/starting tasks, or being frustrated that I forget/missed something.

That said, here are a couple of things to note:
-There are some activities created for you, but to get the most out of it, you’ll need to take the time (and find the motivation) to setup customized tasks.  I think the colors/pics makes that more fun.
-The app is a bit glitchy every now and then. It might not save or has a delay in updating something that I’ve just saved.  Which seems to make the app spasm a bit and I will close and restart it.  It’s not excessive, but no one likes the feeling of “losing their work”.  Hoping these bugs will be fixed to make use more smooth!

All in all, I’m really appreciating this app and think it’s worth it!

author: Ayers5599

title: Almost perfect
body:
I love the idea of this app - everything down from being able to select emojis associated with each task and color code them is BRILLIANT. There was clearly input from the neurodivergent community and for that, I’m so appreciative! I love the notes feature as well - it’s so easy to get all my thoughts outs and then add them as tasks to my schedule later. 

However, the inability to use this app in its full glory across devices is a major downfall. For example, the routines that I create on the mobile app don’t sync onto the desktop version. Since I don’t always have my phone beside me, I often miss when routines begin, when pomodoro goes to break, or when I have an activity scheduled. 

There are also some glitches - for instance when I “pause” an activity it doesn’t actually seem to pause. When I press “start” again it just jumps to wherever it would have been if I’d never paused at all. 

For now I’m switching to another app, that isn’t as cool or as customizable or as detailed as Tiimo, but that is more cohesive across devices. If Tiimo develops a better desktop app that’s just as thorough and syncs up to the mobile app smoothly, I’ll certainly be downloading again. For me, unless I can have it on my personal computer, work computer, iPad, and phone, it just won’t be as effective.
author: smememeyes

title: Can be very helpful, but very buggy and learning curve is not great
body:
I’ve really enjoyed this app and it has helped me out a lot. However, the rigidity of it is very unhelpful for people with ADHD. 

I don’t know if this is a feature and my app is buggy, or if you simply can’t uncheck activities. Sometimes I’ll accidentally check an activity off in a routine and I can’t uncheck it! I’ll have to start the whole routine over to get back. 
This also affects when I go in and add something to a routine already in progress, since tiimo will suddenly skip me like 3 activities. I was barely on my 3rd activity, added one to my routine, and it skipped me to like the 6th. And of course, I couldn’t uncheck the checked activities, so I had to go and delete the routine, add it back, and start it over. 
I also wish we could add more time to an activity already happening. My time blindness makes it hard to figure out how long something will take me, and when I realize something will take me longer than I thought, I have to pause the activity and use an external timer, which mixes me up! Being able to restart an activity already in progress would be good too (sometimes I get distracted and can’t start exactly when it wants, but seeing it already started discourages me from getting back on track. 

I also think that the learning curve is very large, the initial app instructions are vague, and the blog posts linked are too many and too long with not enough screenshots just to get a barebones understanding how the app works. I’ve had more help watching youtubers use it than from the tutorials they have. 

I totally understand this is a work in progress, and I will continue to support the team of course. This has helped me get on track and balance my life much better. But the inflexibility is really frustrating and discouraging.

title: Sanity saver!!!
body: I don’t have an official diagnosis yet, but I have many symptoms of ADHD and just now discovering it in my 30s. I feel like so much of my life has been explained and time management has always been a struggle for me. I work full time, mostly remote, homeschool 2 of our 4 kids so far, and run a small business. I’ve been looking for something like this app for a long time. Paper planners only help for a short period of time for me and then I forget to check it and waste half of it. I love that this fills so many gaps I didn’t know I had or needed - the heads up notifications that a specific routine or activity is about to end or halfway done is awesome. So is the notes area where you can braindump a to do list or anything you want and then actually schedule it straight from there if needed at a later time. The integration with Apple Watch is also awesome bc I can put my phone away and have super focused time but still get the reminders I need (i know you can do focused mode on iPhone, but I’m still tempted to get distracted with my phone nearby). I’ve only had this app for a couple days and am still learning it but will definitely be keeping it past the trial! I love love LOVE this! Thank you so much for putting so much thought and intentionality into Tiimo!
author: TMLwood

title: A lot of potential, needs work
body:
Apple Watch app is basically not functional - can’t check off items, can’t go to the end of an activity (or skip). Doesn’t change between activities when the time runs out. This is a dealbreaker for me personally; I can’t be running to my phone between items in the routine. 

There seems to be some training required to use this app. For example, what on earth is the difference between an activity and a routine? Why can’t I have checklists in a routine? Why can’t activities be a part of a routine?

Excellent idea in this app: the “notes” section and the ability to drop tasks from there into your day. But the keyboard covers the part where you type, so it’s really hard to input tasks. 

I don’t love that the daily calendar UI shows my completed tasks/routines/activities. It creates a lot of confusion when looking at that screen. Would be helpful to have an option to turn this off or at least collapse the items in that section.  It’s also not clear why routines happen at “any time” by default - that seems to defeat the purpose of the calendar view. 

I would love to come back to this app when it can be used from the Apple Watch. I currently use Routinery but was looking for something that is a little more calendar-like so I can schedule around my work calendar. Unfortunately this is just not usable right now.

If you plan a 60 minute task at noon, but hit start early at 11am suddenly the task becomes 120 minutes. That defeats the purpose of starting early. It should keep the same length, just move the time. 

Very buggy app.
author: cocomokie

title: great for autistic/adhd ppl
body: love this app so far! I can tell it’s going to be extremely helpful as I start using it more.
author: hannanabannana1

title: Beyond useless
body: The instructions they provide are flat out wrong the screenshots they show would appear to be from a different version of the app iPhone iPad doesn’t matter. Absolutely no way to set this thing up and there is no Support no one to contact nothing don’t waste your time
author: Luvsports597203

title: Wonderful for ADHD community
body:
Simple to use, fun colors but not to many options… or we’d spend more time making it pretty than doing our tasks haha… and consistent reminders.
I also love the incorporation of articles and suggestions right in the app.
Mostly the fact this app is created and run by neuro divergent folks makes it one I want to give my money to!
author: Marley Hope

title: Very promising! - from a designer with adhd
body:
I like this app but I wish it had more of a calendar view like google calendar does. With the ability to tap and hold your activities and move them to any time you want. This would allow for more flexibly and realistic scheduling. 

Also wish there was a list for groceries that you could import into a grocery store shopping activity. 

A to do list where you can automatically schedule the items into your calendar would be nice. Or set them for tomorrow or any date. Like a quick add type feature without all the fuss. 

I like how you can tap checklist items but I wish the visual feedback was better to make me feel like I completed the activity. Or if the activity greyed out or dissapeared.it doesn’t make me feel like I completed the activity. Also wish that activities without checklists had this same type of feature where they grey out or move to some stickied complete list at the top.
author: jasmynf

title: Credit card required to test drive app before purchase
body: Would you agree to lease a car without ever test driving a car? Would you consider leasing it if you knew you could go back to the dealer within two weeks and return the car? No. You would simply lease the car from a dealer with better business practices rather than hand over your personal and financial data to a dealer who requires you to rely solely on the “hope” that the car is good. Disappointing that this model is even permitted on Apple. Perhaps they will continue tightening their review of products and eliminate the availability of products such as this, that are inherently unfair to the consumer.
author: savvy1consumer

title: Watch Difficulty
body: I love this app and the whole concept. It works perfectly for the app on my iPhone and iPad. The major issue I run into is that the widget on my iPhone I use for an extra visual que and the app on my Apple Watch don’t load properly. My watch is constantly giving me an error reading that it was disconnected somehow and won’t keep up with the schedule. I like to receive my notifications as hepatics on my watch rather than have my phone volume up. This way I stay on track, but doesn’t work if my watch can’t keep up with the schedule.
author: Lois1041

title: WONT DISCLOSE PRICE UNLESS U GIVE PAYMENT INFO FIRST
body: Any app that requires me to give my payment info before I’m allowed to try it I refuse on general principle. You should offer the trial BEFORE asking for us to give you access to our bank! Shameful. Any app who I’ve tried that way has ALWAYS tried to keep charging me after I cancelled. I doubt this is any different. I mean, they don’t even tell you how much it is unless you give your email first!
author: swamplillys

title: Big flaw hinders usefulness
body:
On the plus side this ap is attractive and fairly simple to set up with a little tinkering. I was in love with the idea of creating a block schedule that included a alarms, a visible timer, and checklists. Unfortunately I have found that the ap does not send me notification of scheduled events or tasks and the widget shows I have nothing planned for the day even when I do unless I reset the ap each morning (delete it and load it back onto my phone) and open it up again. That is really unacceptable to me. If an ap is unreliable sending notifications or I have to do something first to get it to send reminders than it is not functioning to help me manage my time. I am missing scheduled events or having to remember everything myself anyway. I guess this probably works fine for people who want to use to schedule time blocks on the fly but if you want to use it to prompt you to keep your schedule it fails. Really disappointing considered this is an ap you pay for.
Edit: after emailing with Tiimo, I was told the inability to send me notifications has to do with a limit set by Apple. While I sympathize that their hands might be tied by some restrictions in the IOS, it is hard to see how their solution - sending no notifications until I have already opened the app that day - is effective. Certainly other apps send me notifications before I have opened them that day - the notifications are WHY I opened those apps. Tiimo seems to have it the wrong way around by insisting you open the app before getting any notifications. 
Ultimately the explanation does not make Tiimo more useful to me, but I appreciate that they attempted to explain their viewpoint.
author: AR Etc

title: Should have read reviews…
body: I was under the impression this app had a 2 week trial period. No, I was charged $25 without even getting a look at the app. Even if I wanted to continue, I can’t because it won’t even let me set up an account. I’m out $25 to stare at an error message.
author: sar747

title: It's changing my life for the better
body: I dreamt about an app like Tiimo but I didn't know it already existed! The visual aids and push reminders to my Apple Watch are game changers. Every day I use it more and get more comfortable with customizing it to fit my life. All I can say is THANK YOU to the creators and the team at Tiimo. Please keep up the great work!
author: abossyguy

title: Best Apple Watch integration on the market
body:
This app should cost significantly more than what they charge - and I would still pay it, happily! If you struggle with focusing throughout the day, breaking down big projects, or are frustrated by poorly designed calendar apps with too many unnecessary features, Tiimo is for you. 

It’s simple. It’s scalable. And it’s pretty to look at, to boot. 

+1 for the support team, too. In my experience, they’re quick to help, knowledgeable, and kind.

Lovely app. Lovely folks.
author: Radtron

title: So grateful for this app
body: I struggle with time blindness and this app is the only thing that’s helped beat it! When I use it on my phone and Apple Watch, my days go SO much more smoothly and according to plan. I’m super grateful to the creators of (and team behind) this amazing app!! Thank you all!
author: Asia Faoro

title: Visual timer is pointless if screen goes dark
body:
This app has good ideas, but it isn’t providing for the main reason I got it, which is to help with my daily routines.
1. There is no way to keep the screen from going dark during the timers, making the nice, helpful countdown visual pointless.
2. If the screen is on, the app gives a nice visual celebration when switching activities, but no noise whatsoever. If the screen is dark, I get a phone notification noise between activities. While doing activities, VISUALS and obvious SOUNDS are essential to know how much time I have left and when to switch to the next thing… especially if distracted or hyperfocused!!!
3. I like that you can schedule routines and they start automatically; however, it just starts in the background with no notifications and I need to remember to open the app to see the timers… which disappear in 1 min when my screen goes dark. And I have turned on every notification option available on the app.

I’m really struggling to understand how this app is helpful for ADHD without these things (unless you have a smart watch, in which case that should be clarified on the info page). It’s disappointing that I paid for a year subscription and now have to go back to setting individual alarms on my phone for these things while searching for a new app.
author: Rinnswimmer

title: Not ADHD friendly
body: The fact that you have to put in billing information right from the start for the free trial makes this not ADHD friendly. We have a hard time remembering to cancel subscriptions before free trials end if we are not satisfied with the product. For a company that’s supposed to be working on helping people with ADHD this method of billing seems exploitative.

title: Great in theory but very buggy
body: I love everything about this app in theory but after my first time using it I’m very disappointed. I took a lot of time to enter several tasks/checklists, and ensured that they were saved and appeared on my schedule- only to have them repeatedly disappear. After re-entering the same tasks three times, I closed the app and reopened to see if this would help. Instead it removed all of my checklists except for one. Again, a great idea that seems to work well for many people, but not a good user experience for me. If these are temporary bugs I would be glad to give the app another shot but if this is a recurring issue then I would not bother.

author: Smollfri

body: This app is pretty cool and works like it’s supposed too, but it is a subscription only app. You can’t access or use any of the features without paying a monthly or yearly fee for it. I dunno why they don’t just make it a paid app.
author: friiiiick

title: Good with the exception of one thing
body:
I love how this app allows you to add tasks to things that you need to get done (so like with breakfast or wind down for bed, it allows you to add each step that needs to get done before accomplishing those things to help make those activities less stressful). I haven’t been able to fully mess around with it to figure out how it fully works but the biggest thing I use it for is to remind myself to breathe throughout the day. I absolutely LOVE that throughout the timer set to do this, it does a countdown until it’s done and even has a celebratory screen halfway through! 
My one thing I found frustrating so far is that every now and then, it’ll sign me out so I don’t receive notifications and wind up not noticing for maybe a day or maybe longer since I often loose track of my days.
author: Forevermuic

title: Comprehensive and fun!
body: I never write reviews but I felt the need to tell people that this app has changed my life. I am a generally disorganized person but this app lays everything out on the table. I went in thinking “I’m not going to know how to do any fancy and specific things to fit my needs as a neuro-divergent person.” But anything I clicked I was able to edit, change, and personalize. It has been a life saver especially the reminders and notifications.
author: morticia's lover

title: (Updated) Only had for two days and it’s amazing
body:
I got this because I was having a really hard time managing my schedule and was falling very behind in my classes. This app is exactly what I’d been looking for and I love it so much! I’m going to be asking my family for a year subscription for Christmas! Update 4/13/21: I’ve had this for a while now and all I can say is that it just keeps getting better! Tiimo’s customer service is so nice and they actually consider what their users want in their app. The latest update is amazing with the ability to have freestanding activities and pause activities, and the way the time setup has changed is so much easier to use! I would recommend Tiimo to anyone who needs a little more consistency in their life. Their price after the free trial is reasonable and you get so much more than you pay for. Thank you Tiimo for being so wonderful!
Update 11/16/21: I’ve had this for about a year now and it’s still super great! They just updated again and it’s even better, I can’t remember what was added but I liked it 😆. Even though it has its occasional bug like any app, Tiimo is just such a life saver. As a senior in high school this year my schedule is crazyyyy. It’s very nice to be able to see my next event in the widget. With any luck I will get a smart watch for Christmas so that I can stay on track even better as I prepare for the transition to College! Shout out to the Tiimo Team for being such lovely people! 50/10 would definitely recommend
author: Hose Water

title: I really want to love this app.
body:
Pluses:
- The Apple Watch complication/app is the best feature. Being able to see my entire schedule and progress and checking things off on my lists without looking at my phone is fantastic. 

Deltas:
- The inability to reorder checklist items while editing routines seems like such a basic feature omission that it’s downright frustrating. Instead I have to create whole new items and delete old ones if I want to make any minor change in list order.
- The fact that “Share your day, tag us” is displayed under My Day and Right Now makes me feel as if the creators are more interested in marketing than developing an app with its users’ best interests in mind. Why would I want to share my day and open another distracting social media app when I’m already struggling to keep my day in order? 
- I wish I had the ability to turn off emoji and color customization for every single item. It feels more like a distraction and extra cognitive load than a useful tool for me.
- The Watch app keeps timing out and needs to log in every so often. Annoying and takes a couple of seconds.
- Updates to routines makes the app hang a few seconds with no indication in the UI.

I could say more but overall the app is just clunky with a convoluted finicky interface and an overemphasis on cute customization. I would really like to see a more streamlined and focused UI and/or better user onboarding/tutorials (without having to read through an overly long blog post). 

I’ll update my review as I continue to try and incorporate it into my daily ADHD routine for the next few days.
author: spiffyXD

title: Great app!
body: I just found this and I already love it. Accidentally logged in “edit mode” and was helped very quickly. Problem solved 🥰
author: Micunowska

title: Love this app, but …
body: This app is absolutely amazing. I loved having all the features on my watch to help keep me on task with things. I have adhd and asd and I loved using this, but unfortunately the app on both my iPhone and watch kept logging me out as soon as my wireless connection disrupted. This was so incredibly frustrating. No hints given here, but my email and passwords are too complicated and long to be forced to enter them continuously. Once this issue is fixed however, I will definitely be back to give 5 stars and subscribe.
author: Mad Max Elle

title: Not intuitive to use. But it’s a good start !
body:
This needs a desktop app.
Access across multiple devices.
Activities and routines are good, but it’s too much detailed sometimes when not needed. But it’s a good one overall.
author: Prasadrak

title: Great if it works
body:
Logs me out on my Apple Watch (I’ve had to log back in anywhere from daily to several times a day  Takes days to erase deleted activities/routines, Doesn’t always send notifications, Doesn’t sync well between iPad, iPhone and Apple Watch I’ve seen people claim you can use a website version on a pc and you really can’t. There’s virtually no features/functionality on the website. Also don’t bother syncing your calendar with it, it will default to the calendar so if you have any all day events in your calendar or have a routine or activity you do during an event, those activities either won’t start or won’t send you notifications. 

When it works it’s amazing. But this is the glitchiest, buggiest app I’ve EVER used
author: Oogabooga! Jeklin

title: No offline use
body: I have autism & ADHD and was so excited to use this app, until I found out it only works when you’re connected to the internet. I spend the vast majority of my time with my phone in airplane mode, and this app not only doesn’t work in airplane mode, it logs me out every single time I open the app while in airplane mode. Unfortunately this makes it useless for me :/
author: Happiness seeker 123

title: Amazing app, needs some work
body: I LOVE how this app is laid out, and how it reminds me of my daily routines and appointments (especially on the Apple Watch), but it is a little buggy. Items will randomly disappear from my calendar view, I will schedule something as recurring and it won’t “take” (I have to try a few times) and it’s ALWAYS logging me out on my watch. It’s bearable enough to keep using it but I hope they work those things out because it’s otherwise perfect and really helped me stay on task.
author: HollyKhayos

title: Improving, but there are still problems
body:
I fully acknowledge that this app is a work in progress, and is getting a little better with every update. But there’s still a perpetual problem where as soon as Tiimo is updated, a new feature is rolled out, bugs are fixed and glitches are patched, there is always another problem or new bugs that come up when it seems to be improving. It’s like one step forward and two steps back. I don’t quite understand that because the concept and design of this app seems pretty simple (although I’m sure there’s more to it under the surface). 

I don’t know, I’m just trying to get through my days, get stuff done and not let ADHD (and what I suspect is ASD) get the best of me. This app helps some, but the benefits kind of become redundant when I have to manually go in and correct things because little bugs in the program throw off my routine. The one I’m the most frustrated with right now is the fact that Tiimo likes to log me out of the app on my Apple Watch randomly - it almost always happens overnight, and it sometimes when I’m in the middle of an active routine, and I don’t realize until more time than I had intended to spend on an activity has passed and then “whoops! I have to enter my log-in information again.” 

If you have ADHD or are on the autism spectrum, you know how frustrating and discouraging interruptions to routine can be, especially in their early stages before you’re fully comfortable with them.
author: CalvinationStation

title: Every update, same problem
body: Every time this app gets updated, I get kicked out. And then I can’t log back in. And then I asked for my password to be requested and I never get the email. Then I have to contact customer service, and they have to manually reset my password but only after going through all the stupid steps that don’t work first. And then it last for three months, and then I get kicked out and have to start all over again. It’s not worth it. I’m so over this.

body: I’m autistic, and this app has been so great in helping me to nail down a consistent schedule for myself and remind myself about thing I would normally forget. I live in a rural area, and I only have service in my bedroom, so if I’m not in there, I don’t get my Tiimo notifications. And I have a really hard time remembering to go back to my room all the time to check my schedule.

author: A. Ruo

title: Super helpful but also glitchy!
body: I love how customizable this app is without being cluttered or hard to understand. It does drive me crazy how glitchy and weird the calendar when scheduling a new activity is—especially if it repeats. I end up with activities on days when I did not set them, the calendar always seems to assume I want to schedule something on a Monday even if I am “on” the day I actually want, and it’s hard to comb through and fix all these errors because there’s no option to see them all laid out. So not very user friendly but conceptually beautiful and has helped me and my poor little ADHD brain out significantly!
author: Catapus

title: The best
body:
as an autistic person with chronic illness, i need reminders to properly take care of myself and function in the best way i can. i’ve tried an incredible amount of apps & methods to make this work but tiimo is by far the most accessible, including the price, which is about what i would spend on a good planner for the year. the app layout is very clean and not overwhelming which i find essential. i love the way you can add emojis & colors for the task icons, though i wish there was a way to customize the theme color. i also find it extremely helpful that you can connect to your calendar app.  i use this feature for my work schedule & appointments. 

i would fully recommend tiimo to anyone who needs a visual idea of their day and/or anyone who relies on reminders to get through each day. this is a great app to support and utilize with great people behind it listening & improving
author: Herfeley

title: Needs different sounds

Other than that, I like making lists soo this helps when I have a lot to do but for routine things like breakfast I never change anyway soo it’s kinda pointless.

title: Great app, hoping for small changes
body:
I don’t have adhd or autism but this app has helped me to reflect and improve on my routines and systems a lot. Only thing is I am unable to use the new Widget functionality on the app which I was looking forward to. I have the latest tiimo version so I’m not sure why it’s not available for my iPhone? But that brings me to my suggestions:

What would really make this app spectacular is if it had 2-way sync with Apple Calendar /Google Calendar and if there was a way to block other apps while using this app. 
2-way sync is important to me because i like my events and routines to be backed in my base calendar which is Google Calendar. And having to switch between the two constantly can be frustrating. Also, my second point kind of relates to the widget feature, as I would like to be focused on only the tiimo activity that’s currently scheduled and not be distracted, but having to open the app each time defeats that purpose. Nevertheless I’m excited for what’s to come feature wise with this app as its grown so much, if these features could also be taken into consideration I’d appreciate
author: habits are a blessing

title: Life Automation
body:
I’m actually really impressed with this application, but at almost 30 a year it’s pricey for an application. Not saying it’s not worth it but I hold it to much higher standards then a free application. 

User Interface / Aesthetic ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
First of all the UI is great. It’s simple, and very personable. You pick your main color as long as light or dark mode. The fonts are sleek and modern. The icons are personable. The user interface takes a little bit to get used to but the whole app follows the same interface motion principles so it’s easy to catch on. 5/5 for the UI.

Organization⭐️⭐️
The organization is okay but there should be much more. I would love to be able to indent checklist items to be under another item. Or even put activities under other activities. 

I got this app in order to automate my life with that I wanted to create a morning routine. In my morning routine I have three activities that have many tasks and are very different. Although yes you could sort with colors I cannot separate the timing, or completion aspects.

I also don’t like or understand the separation of activities and routines. Both are important and need to be done. But when you separate them it becomes confusing.

Also when you have multiple activities some being at a certain time some not it becomes VERY clunky. There’s not a way to my knowledge to condense them down, most of the time you can only see 4 activities at a time making it easy to forget activities at the bottom. When you check off an activity it still stays at the top cluttering up the screen. 

During Activity⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Overall great allows you to separate and see a filling circle as the timer, allows you to check off the tasks and isolate your focus. 

Maybe add an alarm to go off after the activity is complete? There is a notification but it’s not noticeable if actually doing a task. Or even take it a step further and integrate a Spotify API to play your playlist until the activity is done. 

Other addition ideas to make this app better: 
- I noticed there’s no siri or shortcut integration. It would be really cool to be able to program nfc to work with the app 

- add urgency level 

- be able to create a key for the colors and what they represent 

- be able to complete a task throughout multiple days, for example if you have a big project with 10 steps and want to work on it for 30 minutes a day 

I will say that I am still learning the app, and will continue to update this review as I know more (:
author: ashleyjdksoosodjmxlls

title: Huge potential. But quite glitchy.
body:
The layout visually is a dream; all is tidy for glancing at. The potential here is actually huge for what the app sets out to do. Unfortunately it's basically still in a buggy beta mode. Even so, I want to stick around to see if they'll fix the bugs and optimize the vision, because if they do, it could be one of the very best of its category. The blogs are really great, laid out nicely and are informative / interesting. But hopefully the layout will become more intuitive for each section and function so that it won't require a deep dive on how-to this or that.

Issues / Requests:

• Can't reset an activity once it's begun.

• If you adjust the activity order by sliding them into different positions, they will force-reset to the original order if you change apps or close and re-open the app. Other times when the order looks correct, pressing an activity will cause it to glitch back into the original order, revealing you've activated a different activity than it displayed at first.

• Sometimes it won't let you check off an activity.

• I would like to customize a sound for each activity as I read was possible, but I don't see that option through any settings or editing. 

• Would be nice to just tap the activity from the list to view it full screen instead of going to the Right Now section. 

• Accessing the Library through the Library icon (beside the + sign for adding an activity ... kind of unclear unless you accidentally find it) to switch to Routines and/or attempt to create a Routine will result in blanked out options, the inability to return to the Activities list, and / or ultimately a dead end, meaning you'll need to force-quit the app and open it again.

• Would be nice to have a setting for automatically starting an activity from a designated finished activity, so that if you want to tie several together seamlessly you could without breaking focus. I think this might be part of the Routine section under development. 

• Not sure what the Notes section is about. 

Hopefully I don't come across as being too merciless with my critique here, hah! But I do look forward to seeing this app accomplish its potential.

title: Helpful and a little buggy
body:

title: Better than a planner!

author: NoahKale

title: Missed the mark for me
body:
Everybody has already mentioned the good, and I agree with much of it.

The bad: 
- Not at all useful for moderate to heavy time blindness. I set an interval timer to go off every six minutes which sorta keeps me on track… lots of people with time blindness just need that level of nudging. Even being able to set halfway, quarter way, eighth way or whatever notifications would help. One notification when a task is transitioning without any prods about how much time has gone by or whether or not I actually switched tasks will only keep me apprised about what I’ve failed to pay attention to for the past hour. You really need multiple notifications for anything other than extremely light time blindness. If I remembered to look at my device every so often to stay on track then I would need this app.

-Syncing is unreliable. Frankly, this instantly makes the app a non-starter for any professional.

-The scheduling is too rigid. For example, sometimes I don’t know in advance if I’m going to make coffee at home or hit the coffee shop. I should be able to have that still be a block in my morning routine without prescheduling it between taking my meds and checking my email. Editing things is a pain.

-Poor event collision notification

-The event adding/routine-making mechanics are clunky. Took me like an hour to even reason about the best way to structure the first 2 hours of my day using their UI idioms and then when I realize I need to change one thing, I need to manually change every thing before or after that was affected by the change. Given, I’ve been making interfaces for a long time, but I could immediately see several ways to improve the operation dramatically.

-The web interface is seriously hobbled because it’s free, so you have to use the app even though data entry in a device is way slower.

And I just keep thinking… this is supposed to be for people with ADHD? 😕 This app clearly has helped a lot of people, but some of it is downright painful for many members of a target audience.

title: I love this app!!

title: A great concept that needs work
body:
Tiimo has a lot of potential, but falls a bit short in usability for now. Setting up your routine for the day is somewhat clunky, but no doubt improves with practice and customization. I’ve found the app somewhat buggy.

Things have disappeared from my schedule. Adding activities and lists is a bit difficult. The keyboard covers the part of the screen where you’re typing the next list item, and emojis/symbols don’t consistently load. Though I have notifications turned on, Tiimo has not notified me of anything. This makes it difficult to see how this is actually useful for time management. For example, I was using the pomodoro routine today, and nearly worked through a break I’d been waiting for. Tiimo wouldn’t allow me to adjust the break time, instead either pushing ahead or requiring me to pause the whole routine.

I feel like this app could be very useful, but with the existing bugs, I don’t find it worth the subscription price. I’ll keep checking in as it progresses. For now, my search for the ideal ADHD app continues.

title: Great start, will stick around for more…
body:
I enjoy that this app gives me a visual schedule of my day.  There are some features that I really feel are missing: 
1. Drag and drop to adjust times of routines or activities. Calendar items would be locked/static and then tasks can shift around as needed between scheduled events. 
2. Visual representation of gaps in the day. I like how the Structured app does this. It shows how much time there is between tasks/events on your schedule and asks if you would like to add anything.  Also their time blocks(bubbles) are larger or smaller based on the length of the task/event. 
3.  Option to add routines to schedule based on end time rather than start time.  This takes away the headache of doing the mental math of trying to plug tasks/routines into my schedule. For example I want to leave the house or be in bed by a certain time and that changes from day to day. I would like to be able to set my morning / evening routines accordingly. Or have my afternoon chore routine complete by the time I start cooking dinner. 
I’m looking forward to seeing what’s next!

author: kenniejeon

title: Wife with Autism, Husband on Night Shift
body:
This app is a lifesaver. My husband’s work schedule shifts between 12 hour day and night shifts. I have a solid day routine but when he works nights, I fall apart. I don’t know when to sleep, eat, do household chores, make dinner, etc. Enter Tiimo. 

A neurodivergent creator on TikTok recommend this app so I gave it a try. I sat down and thought out a routine for when he works on night shift and also a routine for when he has a day off but still needs to stick to his night shift sleeping schedule. It’s been amazing so far. No more oversleeping on my part while getting nothing done and he’s been sleeping a full 8 hours. Meals have been on time and the house is clean! My night shift dread and anxiety has finally gone away. I’m actually thinking about buying an Apple Watch so I can have my routine on my wrist at all times. 

Thank you so much for developing this app. No other time blocking or scheduling software has worked for me in the past. I Bullet Journal, but again, it’s not quite as effective as seeing my routine in real time and being able to be reminded of what I’m supposed to be doing. 
This app will change lives.

Hoping they get it.

author: Auserie Boling

title: figure it out
body: what a disappointment. super glitchy. i created an account, set my theme, explored the nooks and crannies of the app and was very excited to use it. i immediately added a task, created the checklist, selected a cute icon and color, and pressed start. swiped over to the "right now" tab and was delighted with the visually appealing timer, with my tasks clearly laid out in front of me. i got to work right away. ten minutes later, i looked up to see a black screen. the app had suddenly closed, and logged me out. i tried fruitlessly to log back in, multiple times. i restarted the app. i restarted my phone. eventually i deleted the app and redownloaded it to see if it would help. each time i tried to log in, i received an html error code, or an error that said "user could not be authenticated" or something like that. what the heck. after digging through some reviews, i see that this is not an uncommon problem. this unfortunate error totally disrupted my workflow, and i am frustrated with this outcome. all i can say is i am so glad there was a free trial option so i didn't waste my money on this app. great concept, poor execution. i will check back in a few months once the developers have gotten help and worked out some of the serious bugs & kinks!

body: Thank you for making this app. I am autistic and have a degree of adhd to top it off. This app really helped me finally feel grounded. I have tried many schedule apps and have struggled. author: Lake Hylia

title: FANTASTIC app & have suggestions!
body:
This app is the best scheduler for me, especially since I can make a widget on my Home Screen to remind me of what I need to do whenever I pick up my phone. Combined with reminder notifications, this 100% prevents me from forgetting stuff! And I LOVE having the ability to designate certain tasks as things that can be done anytime during the day (I’ll call these Anytime Activities).

My only qualm is that Anytime Activites don’t show up in the Right Now view or in the Widget. So here’s a feature/tweak I would love to see: a button to show/hide Anytime Activities in the Right Now view, along with an option in Settings to set whether Anytime Activities are displayed in the Widget. That way, people who like how it functions right now can keep it like that.

Anyway, my favorite part about this app is that the Widget displays bright colors and pictures that I can’t overlook on my Home Screen. Tiimo is fantastic and I’m excited to see it continue to improve!

I can actually schedule things without a time so I can put all my business tasks I need to get done there for the day. And I can still schedule my meals and appointments to the hour.

author: aWyldeHeart

title: Does NOT help w/ ADHD
body: It’s a lovely concept, but the app is NOT helpful for ADHD. People with ADHD struggle with time blindness, meaning they underestimate the amount of time it takes to do a task. So you end up not done with something you scheduled, and the app is already promoting you to begin the next task. Also, people with ADHD struggle to start tasks and stay on track, but the app only sends one reminder at start time and end time. Suggestion: for ADHD, the app should send multiple reminders to keep us on track. Also, there should be the option to extend the amount of time for a task and automatically move up the other task (except for fixed time tasks like meal times and appointments).
author: ashleyk11

title: Love this App
body: I’ve tried out just about every planner app there is to offer and this is the only one that works for me. Can’t wait to see the great this the developers are going to do in the future with Tiimo!
author: cemu99

title: I love this! Two suggestions though
body: I’m autistic and I love this app! I get depressed when I don’t have an externally imposed routine and this helps create that for me and literally avoid depression! I love the interface and the colors. Two ideas: color themes - you can pick in the settings which color scheme you’d like and then when you select the color for an event it gives you those colors as options. For example I love neon colors or pastels and I wish it let me pick one of those as a theme so I didn’t have to build a bunch of custom colors. Second idea: make the ability to not give a task a duration. Sometimes it gives me anxiety to put a duration on something that I don’t know how long it’ll take. On these tasks we could simply check them off when we’re done. It would ease a lot of stress in creating schedules.

title: A Game-Changer

I love how this app is easy to navigate with endless customization options, and I’ve recommended it to people of all ages. It doesn’t feel like I’m using an app made for a toddler, and even my neurotypical friends say that the format has helped them too.

Bonus points for being a small company run by neurodiverse individuals and for an engaging blog presence touching on a variety of important topics. Worth every single cent.

title: I looooove Tiimo!
body: I love my paper planners, but if I forget to look at them for a few days, I lose all sense of time. I’m always on my phone though, so this is perfect, and better than alarms I immediately ignore because they’re annoying. The way reminders are set up in this app really helps me keep on track. I love the visual layout, and how customizable it is, it makes me WANT to open the app, and the widget for my home screen is so appealing. I’m still playing around with how I use it, but overall really enjoying it so far! And I love seeing how Tiimo listens to users, and makes timely updates to better suit our needs. I’ll report back in a few months to see if I keep using it!

author: Jacob E Hartman

title: I really want to like this
body:
I really want to like this app, so much so that I paid for a year upfront without reading any reviews. My bad. I like the look of it, and I like the idea, but actually using it is way more complicated than it needs to be.

Problems I’ve run into in my first 24 hours:
-can’t click and drag checklist items
-an item I allotted 30 minutes for keeps resetting to 24hrs 30min
-can’t reorder activities on iPhone that are set to “any time”
-when viewing the calendar on desktop (chrome) that I created on iPhone, only one activity shows up for today and it’s one I’ve already completed. The other activities I have scheduled for today are not shown.
-when I add an activity to my day on desktop, it still does not show on desktop (I can only see the same one completed activity as before), but it does appear on iPhone.
-on desktop I cannot zoom out to view a whole week, I can only see 4 days at a time. I also cannot zoom in to see just today.
-on the other side of that coin, on iPhone I cannot zoom out to see more than one day at a time.
-if an activity is not assigned assigned a specific time, and it is checked off, I feel it should go to the bottom of the day. Instead it still takes up a bunch of space in the middle of the day even though I no longer need to think about it.
-on my “right now” view on iPhone, the description spot for one activity shows the description I put for a different activity. Both activities show the same description. When I return to “my day” the descriptions show correctly. Unpausing and re pausing the activity switches which description shows on both activities (most recently active shows on both).

The desktop calendar is totally unusable for me, and the iPhone app is... usable but barely. I hope to see these issues fixed, because if this system works properly, I would love to use it and don’t mind paying for it. But for now, I can’t recommend it.

Edited to add: less than three hours after submitting this review I now receive an error message logging in. After logging in, I am offered the various subscription plans, even though I already purchased an annual subscription. Logging out and logging back in, restoring purchase, nothing works. When I click restore, it says there is a problem retrieving the receipt. I can no longer access my account on iPhone, which is the only platform it was even half useful on for me. I have now cancelled my subscription within the free trial period.

If I hear that these functionality issues have been addressed, I would love to subscribe again and would be happy to pay for an app like this. Hopefully I will still be able to do a free trial next time, as I have seen enough for now to know this isn’t going to work without some serious updates, but would want to try out a future version before committing again.

author: KCKMom

title: so far amazing with a few suggestions
body:
my reasoning:
- when i save a routine and try to add it to another day it only adds a portion of the routine (like for my getting ready to leave i have things like get dressed, pack bag, and brush teeth but it only added get dressed when i tried to add the routine). it would also be great if you could make the routine feature have a way to add one activity at a time but still have all the activities stores under the same routine. allowing editing of the activities while it’s in the routine as well would fantastic as well. 
- there needs to be a way for the activity log to have two sorting options: name and time frame. i usually put in my classes and such at the beginning of each term yet sometimes things change and i need to add an additional class meeting for say finals or something but i can no longer find that activity i created at the beginning of the month. that means i have to recreate it and go back to find what color i labeled it with and such yet i have about 15 “shower” blocks in a row in the activity tab because i shifted the time frame of those most recently and that feels excessive and unproductive. there needs to be a way to save one of each activity i create under its name and disregard the timing/frequency it’s used. please add a subsection of the activity log that has one of each activity i’ve created sorted alphabetically by name and if you really want to make me happy add a search feature to that section as well.
- would really like a feature that allows me to schedule time to take my medicine during other activity without the app and website freaking out that i overlapped the times every time i open the planner. it’s so nice when i make planning mistakes but i don’t want to have two homework blocks surrounding the reminder to take my medicine especially since i can’t alter the notifications for each specific activity. so really this is two suggestions: 1. allow me to signal to the system that i know things are overlapping for certain activities and it’s okay and 2. let me alter the notifications for the start/end of each individual activity. the notification settings across the app determine default notifications but i can choose to change them for individual activities as well. 

i hope the future holds partnerships that help make this app free for the portions of the neurodivergent community who can’t afford the fee.
**this is an updated review after using the app for a month as of 3/9/2021
author: keriwozz

title: I have been waiting for this app for ages, but it’s green
body:
I have literally been waiting for an app like this (that allows for some sort of integration of my events, tasks, and general time keeping) for ages. I know there are apps out there that already do something like this, and some of them do portions of it somewhat well, but they generally are extremely clunky, convoluted and somehow manage a mix of too many and at the same time not enough customization (🤷‍♂️). 
And when I refer to the blend of those items it is often best if the app can just pull in from existing sources (easy for calendars, often not so easy for tasks). 

So when I saw Tiimo, what it could do, the fact that it *looked* pleasing/had a nice UI AND had an Apple Watch app?! Heck yes, definitely wanted to try it. As the app is only a few months old I’m not surprised there are some gaps, but based on what I’m seeing the developers are working hard to fill them!

I noticed that they are working on adding tasks with no fixed start/end time (currently you can only add a task to a specific date, with a specific start and end time. And from there your only quick option is to start the task) & they are adding a search feature to the task list (you can add common tasks that you perform to a template list & they have a fairly well populated pre-made template list as well!). 

I’m not sure how it would fit in with the changes being made, but as one who subscribes to the GTD method what I really would need to have to keep using the app is an ‘inbox’. Sometimes I just need to jot down my tasks so I don’t forget what they are, other times I have enough, well, time to fully detail/log the task and when I want to do it. 
I was thinking of just putting them in the templates list, but this would just get really really cluttered without a way to differentiate between the two (keeping in mind, the whole point of the inbox is to add quickly so adding a color or other flag to inbox items would sort of defeat the purpose). 
And with the ability to not have a fixed start/end time it would be nice to have some sort of ‘auto scheduler’ - whether it’s ‘I have x amount of free time & I am in Y location (and ideally with Z contexts as filters 😉), what can I get done? Or just a more basic one with the app noticing you have free time and suggesting to add items from your inbox to your schedule. 

Anyway - great app so far! Definitely going to keep an eye on it!
author: appoli13

title: I adore this app
body:
This app is amazing for me as someone with ADHD. The visual timer with the added notifications for beginning, halfway, and end of a task really ease any anxiety that comes from wondering how long I’ve been doing a thing. 

The only addition I would ask for is a sort of “nag” function. Maybe it asks if I want to start every x amount of minutes and won’t until I say yes? I have a bad habit of seeing the event start and if I’m not quite ready, it leaves my mind. But if I could maybe add 5min and it asks me again, or similar, it’s much easier for me to remember and get started on my task because it won’t allow me to forget.

Thank you so much for this app. Life is a little less chaotic with it

title: Lovely app except some glitches.
body:
Great visual time keeper great for my ADHD. 

For some reason, almost every button has been seemingly shortened. For example, when I go to add a task, Why is “add time” shortened to “ad...time” ? This is frustrating and makes it take more cognitive effort to figure out what’s going on. Must be a glitch, could be solved by allowing users to adjust the text size themselves which might also increase accessibility. 

Also, please add the ability to collapse calendar notes. The automatic Zoom calendar invite comes with soooo much info that when automatically displayed in tiimo, it takes so much time to get an overview of my day. 

Overall, great app. I think if you could improve “glance-ability” or the ease at which I can concisely understand what’s going on, this app would truly shine.
author: Booberrox392

title: A little glitchy
body:
Hi,

A disclaimer: I just downloaded the app yesterday so I may not know how to navigate it yet fully. I added Tiimo as a widget and I wanted to be able to see what I need to be doing at a glance without opening the app. However, it has had the same display message yesterday saying “This was it for today, see you tomorrow 👋” when I still had an activity to do. The widget had worked properly when the Tiimo sign up activity occurred, but not now. I thought maybe the problem was that the activity I had scheduled was between two days of the week (10 pm - 1 am). But I adjusted the time to 10 pm - 11 pm and the message didn’t show up either. I also turned notifications on (I had turned all of them off because the widget would work just fine for me) but that didn’t solve the problem either. I was able to get the notification on my iPhone’s home screen, but the widget still said the “This was it for today, see you tomorrow 👋”.  Also, when I checked the app to see what was going on, it said my activity was already over, which is not true since it just started when the notification popped up. Therefore I can’t see the visual timeline of how long I have until my activity is over, because it claims it already happened. I would like to use Tiimo for that purpose of letting you visually see how much time you have left, I think that would really help me out. But I can’t see it using the widget or when I open the app. I rated 5 stars because the app is really cool and it has a lot of potential. Also this is super super nit picky (I have OCD in addition to the reasons why I use this app 🙄), but if there was a way to delete “My icons” from the photo menu, that would be cool too because I selected something that I didn’t want for an activity one time and now I have to see it every time I go to set a picture for an activity. That is probably the last priority on your update list but I just thought I would mention it. Thank you so much for all your hard work!

body: This tool has a lot of great features. I just started using and am just learning my way around. For example, I would prefer to have an entry that says “workout (6a-7a)” that within you could establish “stretch 6-6:10, cardio 6:10-6:40, cool down 6:40-7.” The only options I see are to either create new entries for each, or do one entry and use the checklist. author: trell4real

title: Mixed bag
body:
There are a lot of things I love about this app. The graphics the visual design the use of checklists to make sure I don't forget things. I love the reminders. 

Two things in particular really bother me though. The limited smart watch compatibility which means I'm being forced to choose between app compatibility and other key functions I want like stress monitoring which I could have with a fitbit. I don't like the notifications directly on my phone because it forces a distraction I don't need. Also I might leave my phone beside my bed to go brush my teeth and wash my face so the app doesn't work as well without a watch.

I'm also struggling to connect to the web calender. I work nights and can't get any customer service and the faq/help sections are a joke tbh. I'm super stressed trying to deal with it which is kind of counter productive. It also won't accept my password which I had saved and apparently fixing this issue isn't as easy as submitting a request either. I can't view any account information on the app either including what email I might have signed up with.

Overall I'm only giving it 3 because I really like the functionality of the app but the other issues have me reaching for my anxiety meds because I'm 90 minutes in and I've made 0 progress with little hope of help in the foreseeable future.

author: Cams🖤

title: Love this app!
body:
I absolutely love this app, it is pretty much exactly what I’m looking for.  I do have a few requests that I think would really help me and maybe others. 

1. The only thing I don’t like about this app is the way the notifications work.  As someone who hyper fixates on things the quick ding isn’t enough to get my attention and move on to the next task.  If there is some way where there could be an alarm sound (maybe as an option if others don’t want it) or to have the phone vibrate for a few seconds.  I just need it to last longer than the typical “ding” and I can’t find a way to do it in settings for just this app.  I’m not sure if there’s a way to fix this within development, but even a sound or vibration that goes off while in the app would be helpful.  I could just leave the app open while doing my work. 

2. I would also love the option to have more flexibility with the day.  Although I definitely understand that many people using an app like this are using it for structure, I would like the option to have scheduled tasks and unscheduled tasks.  This way I don’t have to make it so minute to minute.  So basically I would be able to have “study” and I could set it for an hour duration but not have to schedule it for a specific time.  When I feel like studying I could click “start studying” and it would set an hour timer or something.  I have ADHD and get distracted very easily so the whole minute to minute planning doesn’t always work since I end up falling behind.  I think having the option to not schedule every task for an exact time would be perfect for me.

author: syd01!

title: I LOVE this app, but there are a couple kinks
body:
As someone who is neurodivergent, this app has helped me bring order and structure to what was an overwhelming amount of unstructured time. I highly recommend trying it for a couple weeks if you think you’ll benefit, because you’ll probably find it as helpful as I did.

Now for why I docked a star: there are a couple of things that could really improve the app. A search feature for the icons would streamline use. More background colors as well (especially a white background option) would be nice, as I’ve found I run out of color coding colors quickly. Also, being able to schedule multiple things at one time (such as eating lunch while at work) and being able to more easily repeat activities on the same day (rather than just the next day/ week at the same time) would be great for those of us who take meds more than once daily and while doing other things. Finally, adapting the app to be available to sync on the smarter FitBit devices would be VERY helpful (I’d gladly pay a fee to download it onto my device if that’s what it takes). Though these would make the app better and more useful, it’s already pretty great, so if I had the option to give it 4.5 instead of 4, I would have.

author: Tiger_on_the_Keys

title: No Other App Compares
body: I’ve used almost every single planner app that’s free on the appstore or has a free trial and if you have Autism or ADHD/ADD - this planner is for you. As much as I live the idea of using paper planners, my brain physically can’t handle it. I wish it was 100% free, BUT they are working on three different ways to make it so, one being possibly partnering with a research institution (vetted for ethics) for those 18+ to submit a small survey to unlock months of free Tiimo! author: Elle🦁🐶🐝🐙(munchkiiwii)

title: Unintuitive, missing basic functionality, buggy
body:
If you look at the help guide on iPad in landscape mode, the top section of text isn’t visible, but there’s no indication that it’s cut off, so you just see a strangely unhelpful series of images without context — until you get to the final screen where the image overlaps the text and it looks like the app is just badly designed. 

When you tap the plus button, there are three options that appear. But for some reason only one option appears first and the other two are withheld for a second, so it’s easy when you’re starting out or are in a rush to tap the pill thinking it will open a submenu. In other words the interface can trick you into choosing the wrong function every time you tap the plus button.

If you try to create a routine but you haven’t created activities yet, you will get a blank-ish screen with instructions to create an activity, with an arrow that points to a blank space. Tapping the blank space does nothing—in other words, the plus button isn’t just invisible, it’s completely missing. There is no way to create a routine until you create activities first. 

You’re forced to assign starting times to everything you create. What if I want to create a daily routine with a variable start time? I don’t want to see an indicator that I’m “late” to start the routine, and I don’t want alerts telling me to start it before I’m ready. I just want to know that the daily routine is waiting for me to start it when I’m ready. This app won’t let you use routines in that way. 

On top of all of that, the developer asks that you create an account and hand over personal information BEFORE you can even test it! 

Those are all CONS. Usually in a review you’d also list PROS but any pros I can find are so trivial compared to all of the problems listed above that I don’t want to include them for fear of giving someone the wrong impression that the good counterbalances the bad.

Stay far away from this app in its current state. It will not help you.

title: It just works
body:

My first impression wasn’t so great though. Why aren’t there streaks, graphs, badges, statistics, and other useless vanities? Because they’re distractions.

The simplicity of the app keeps you focused on getting the next task done and not sweating any of the unimportant details.

There’s no “delay this task for 10 minutes button” or any of that other garbage that helps you procrastinate — remember that this is for people who may have trouble with organization and procrastination.

There are definitely some things I would improve and some other things I would add but all in all it works.

Cheers, Tiimo! 

I had ADHD and I heard that Tiimo is a great app for your schedule so I downloaded it and it’s almost perfect, but there’s one feature that makes it frustrating for me to use. When I’m creating a routine or activity I want to be able to use the length of time an activity takes instead of a start and stop time. It might seem small, but I have time blindness so I time myself doing activities and record the amount of time they take to complete. Then I use that to schedule. Ideally I would place it on my schedule at the time I want to start and the end time would generate. With the start and stop time, whenever I want to place an item on my schedule at a different time it’s frustrating to first determine the amount of time the task takes, then reset the start and end time. Otherwise I really enjoy this app.

title: Updating my review
body:
I’m updating my review again from 3 stars to 4. The app has improved since I started using it, and some of the bugs have been worked out. One issue I reported was fixed within a couple of days. Also, one issue that I assumed was a bug went away when I upgraded to a newer iPad. I can see that the developers are really making an effort to make the app better. 

This is a very unique app, and I haven’t found another like it. I have ADHD and autism, and it works with the way my brain works. I have executive dysfunction, and I have a hard time getting started on tasks. Seeing the notification that a task is about to start kind of creates a sense of urgency to get started. And it keeps me on task. And because I’m a visual thinker, I like that you can customize the color and icons. Calendars have never worked for me, partly because you can never exactly guess how long a task will take and unexpected things come up. This app is flexible in that it lets you start and finish tasks early or late. So it’s pretty cool, and I think it helps me a lot.

title: Awesome potential, some bugs still need working out
body:

When the app requested permission for my photos, I changed my mind and wanted to go back to the built in icon options. So I tapped on the x for the request camera/gallery access window, but instead of collapsing the window it just regenerated the same window. Also, it’d be really cool to have overlapping events show a visual depiction of the time overlap instead of a warning (if that makes sense...?). author: TheGeek65

title: Top notch privacy policy - please add audible reminders
body:
Tiimo Privacy policy is the best. Don’t let people steal & sell your kid’s information for a cheap app! 

Easy to use, add your repeating or single events, choose icon & colour. Determine if event can start or end early. It reminds with a banner and shows the amount of time remaining. Swipe to end early.

I decided not to keep this app because it doesn’t have audible alarms. This app is for someone who is willing to monitor their own device for reminders, not for the easily distracted or those that need constant reminders.

Please add audible alarms! Banners are not enough for distracted kids. Screaming monkeys, tiger roars or mom’s recorded (pleasant, not screaming) voice are all acceptable options. 

Please add secondary (optional) distraction alarm that can beep every n minutes for easily distracted kids. 

These 2 things are all this app needs to put parents out of the nagging business!

title: Crashes all the time, notification never work, etc.
body:
I wanted really like this app, but it constantly crashed and gives me a database error. This error didn’t seem to effect anything so I figured eventually it would be fixed.

The app’s notifications would also seem to just stop. I would actually forget all about it at times because it doesn’t function the way the way you expect it to, and those expectations are formed from the developers description. I figured I would keep using it and subscribe. I figured maybe I didn’t set it up correctly. BUT.... I ended up cancelling  my subscription once I realized that I would have to manually manipulate the data to account for Daylight Saving Time (USA).

I still have access because I already paid for the year...so maybe the issues will get fixed?

author: @gilliancookstudio

title: Completely useless without a subscription—major paywall trap
body:
Don’t waste your time downloading this if you are looking for a free scheduling tool. They market it as a visual planner, but they lock the most basic, non-negotiable features behind a subscription wall.
You cannot repeat a task across multiple days. You cannot copy a day's schedule. You can't even duplicate a basic routine without being prompted to buy the premium version. The built-in AI assistant completely freezes or goes blank if you try to give it a standard calendar prompt, making it completely pointless.
Forcing users to manually type out every single task from scratch every single day just because they don't want to pay a subscription is ridiculous. There are plenty of other calendar and timeline apps out there that let you use basic repeat and copy functions for free. Skip this one.
